samples.book: 042 - Supervillains and Philosophy - Sometimes, Evil Is Its Own Reward
samples.relation: Three 'Phase Four' essays. Moseley reads the Joker across Batman #1, The Killing Joke, The Dark Knight, A Death in the Family, and Dark Knight Returns as a 'moral monster' who knowingly does evil - and, following Anscombe and Scanlon's guise-of-the-good analysis, pursues aesthetic 'higher values' in a Camus-like affirmation of the absurd, embracing the irrationality Batman's rational moral order cannot fathom. Levin uses X-gene biology (Beast's explanation in Astonishing X-Men, genotype vs phenotype, M-Day) to strip Magneto's Homo sapiens superior claim of any genetic or phenotypic basis, then argues via the moral community of rational persons (Kant's criterion) that mutants and humans share one moral community, condemning both the Registration Act and mutant separatism. O'Neil's prose piece traces Harvey Dent from Calvinist certainty through the acid that scars him to cosmic doubt - quantum randomness, many worlds, Sartre's condemnation to freedom - until Nietzsche's amor fati lets him embrace duality and let the scarred two-headed coin decide good and evil.

samples.book: 043 - The Golden Compass and Philosophy - God Bites the Dust
samples.title: The Golden Compass and Philosophy
samples.relation: Auxier argues the trilogy is narrated on a Nietzschean lattice rather than being a mere inverted Milton: after tracing the Paradise Lost, Genesis 6, and Pseudepigrapha sources (Azazel as the model for Asriel, Metatron from Third Enoch, Dust from Milton's warring particles), he reads Mrs. Coulter's speech to Father MacPhail about seeking God out and giving him 'the gift of death' as Nietzsche's death of God fused with a description of Nietzsche's own final dementia. Will and Lyra become overman and overwoman beyond good and evil: Will rises by his will and his willingness to kill (the alethiometer's verdict 'He is a murderer' makes him a worthy companion), while Lyra commands both truth and lies, the alethiometer embodying truth as 'a mobile army of metaphors.' But the chapter's payoff is critical: Pullman does not endorse Nietzsche, since in a world where the will to power dominates, the overwoman Mrs. Coulter has no place and falls with Asriel and Metatron into the Abyss, while Xaphania's teaching offers a disciplined, workful imagination as an alternative.

samples.book: 099 - Louis C.K. and Philosophy - You Don't Get to Be Bored
samples.title: 1. Everything’s Amazing and Nobody’s Happy
samples.relation: Max Elder reads Louis through Nietzsche's Gay Science claim that all philosophy is unconscious memoir, arguing Louis's confession-like comedy reveals dark truths we would rather flee - the Conan 'everything's amazing and nobody's happy' bit, the 'I know the darkness' exchange with the Christian woman, and the Subway/Pamela scene where a homeless man bathes behind a subway violinist. Using Nietzsche's line that man alone laughs because he suffers so deeply, and The Birth of Tragedy's comic as the artistic discharge of the nausea of absurdity, the chapter argues Louis's laughter performs a gestalt switch that ties the ugly to the beautiful and so redeems it. It reads the religions-supply-meaning argument - God's mockery-laughter versus Nietzsche's holy laughter - as the reason redemption now happens in comedy clubs rather than churches, and closes with Louie's 'Country Drive' scolding of Jane ('you don't get to be bored') as Nietzschean embrace of the amazing fact of being alive.

samples.book: 170 - House and Philosophy - Everybody Lies
samples.title: Notes
samples.relation: Argues against the title claim of the previous chapter: Frank is a Nietzschean master type — he defines good as good-for-him, embraces pain as strength, and keeps no allegiances once Walker and Vasquez break their promise — while Peter Russo is the paradigmatic reactive slave who cannot command himself and blames others, exactly Nietzsche's 'he who cannot command himself is commanded'. But the overman requires self-overcoming, the sublimation of drives into creation, and amor fati, and Frank only dominates others for vengeful ends: his whole scheme grows from ressentiment over the Secretary of State snub, he affirms other wills merely as investments, and in Season 3 he becomes a slave to his own position. The chapter uses the Cesare Borgia misreading (better a Borgia than a Parsifal as raw material, but Borgia was no overman), Napoleon's corruption, and Goethe's creative wholeness to conclude that Frank remains 'all-too-human' — destruction without creation.

samples.book: 068 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Zombie Apocalypse Now
samples.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
samples.relation: Rard tests whether objective morality survives the apocalypse by running four theories against Season Two: Plato's Forms explain universal truths about walkers ('walkers survive so long as their brains are relatively undamaged') but cannot handle white lies or changed circumstances, and Aristotle's virtue ethics reads Rick's rush from the shot Carl as rashness and Shane's supply run as courage, yet virtues prove relative and luck-dependent in a collapsed world. Natural law founders on clashing intuitions — Merle's racism and Hershel's barn of walkers each claim self-evidence. The chapter's center is Nietzschean: Hershel's barn is slave morality that pities the 'sick,' Maggie breaks from it, and Shane's sacrifice of Otis and opening of the barn enact a will-to-power master morality without joy, while Rick alone moves toward amor fati — embracing the world as it is, refusing guilt over Lori's affair, and insisting the baby be born into the Walk Age.

samples.book: 073 - The Wire and Philosophy - This America, Man
samples.title: The Wire and Philosophy
samples.relation: Brittingham argues The Wire is a Nietzschean rather than merely Aristotelian tragedy, a wrestling between the Apollonian orientation of order, statistics, and illusion (Rawls's clearance rates, Burrell's bureaucracy, Stringer's business plans) and the Dionysian reveling in the Game's chaos and suffering (Avon accepting that 'you only gotta fuck up once', McNulty's intoxicated self-destruction). Stringer is Nietzsche's 'theoretical man' whose faith that thought can correct existence, embodied in the New Day Co-Op, cannot save him from Omar's 'It ain't about money', while McNulty is the Dionysiac man inside the Apollonian institution until Freamon's 'the job will not save you' forces his resignation. The chapter closes by reading the characters' resigned embrace of their fates as Nietzschean affirmation: since neither the job, intelligence, violence, nor the gods will save you, the only response is to say yes to life anyway.

samples.book: 189 - The Ultimate Star Trek and Philosophy - The Search for Socrates
samples.title: Notes
samples.relation: Argues Q embodies Nietzsche's revaluation of values: contemptuous of herd-like safety, Q subjects Picard and the crew to trials ("Encounter at Farpoint", "Hide and Q", "All Good Things"'s "the trial never ends") meant to force growth beyond conventional morality, seek out other "supermen", and embrace risk - Q's "bloody nose" defense after eighteen crewmen die at the Borg in "Q Who?". The Borg figure as everything Nietzschean individualism despises, a mindless collectivism that robs drones of the passion the strong need to individuate, and Q's offer to join Picard as guide pictures a friendship between Nietzsche's self-mastered few. The lesson of "Tapestry" is amor fati: Picard must embrace the Nausicaan knife fight that nearly killed him, since undoing it makes a safe, unnoticed man - though the authors finally refuse Nietzsche's harsher dictum that the weak should perish, siding with healing over Q's education-by-death.

samples.book: 093 - More Doctor Who and Philosophy - Regeneration Time
samples.title: 14. The Doctor’s Desire for Human Suffering
samples.relation: Cooper reads 'Rise of the Cybermen' and 'The Age of Steel' as staging Nietzsche against Mill's pain-eradicating utilitarianism: John Lumic, who builds the Cybermen to abolish his sickness, exemplifies the life-denying herd—losing his creativity, craving 'unity and uniformity,' becoming 'a living brain with a heart of steel'—while the Doctor, answering that a life without pain would be 'you might as well kill me,' affirms suffering as the source of creativity, striving, and strength. She extends the Nietzschean reading to the Doctor's character: his guilt over the Time War double-genocide and his loneliness ('the only certainty left is that you'll end up alone') become the pain that makes him merciful, from offering Dalek Caan compassion after 'Evolution of the Daleks' to forgiving the Master in 'Last of the Time Lords,' so that mercy is, as the Genealogy of Morals says, 'the privilege of the most powerful man.'

samples.book: 172 - The Hunger Games and Philosophy - A Critique of Pure Treason
samples.title: The Hunger Games and Philosophy
samples.relation: Jason Eberl treats the muttations, jabberjays that mimic speech without understanding, tracker jackers, the wolf-mutts with Glimmer's eyes that torment Cato, and the lizard-mutts hissing Katniss's name, alongside real chimeras (geeps, the SCID-hu mouse, Balaban's quail-chick brain transplants, Weissman's human-neural mouse) to ask whether biotechnology could create a person. Working through Boethius's definition of a person as an 'individual substance of a rational nature' and Locke's 'thinking intelligent Being' that can consider itself the same over time, he argues that human DNA alone confers no personhood, while a chimera genuinely capable of self-conscious rational thought would be a person whose weaponized creation and lab captivity would violate its rights, which is why ethicists allow mouse chimeras but hesitate with primates. He notes that the Gamemakers' refusal to see tributes as persons is exactly the move that made slavery and Nazi dehumanization possible, and that Katniss's suspicion about whether the mutts remember their deaths is the right ethical question to keep open.

samples.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
samples.title: Chapter 34 - Beyond Lies the Wub
samples.relation: Dick's first published story dramatizes the moral status of a rational nonhuman: Peterson's wub, a telepathic, philosophical Martian pig-creature, reads minds, discusses Odysseus and individuation, and pleads that it is 'a sensible being like yourselves', yet Captain Franco - obsessed with eating it - freezes it mid-sentence, shoots it looking him in the eye ('Back on the farm we had hogs'), and serves it for dinner, dismissing Peterson's grief with 'It is only organic matter, now.' The wub's personhood is established entirely through language and philosophy, but speech fails to protect it from being treated as meat, and the closing irony - Franco resuming the wub's own Odysseus meditation, as if the mind survived its meal - underscores how thin the line is between person and livestock. The story thus stages the problem of other minds and the ethics of killing sentient beings who demand to be addressed eye-to-eye rather than dined upon.

samples.book: 144 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Knowledge Here Begins Out There
samples.title: Hedging Our Bets
samples.relation: Kind asks whether the Fleet's treatment of Cylons (Roslin airlocking Leoben, Fisk's 'you can't rape a machine,' Cally's killing of Boomer charged as mere discharging of a firearm) presupposes that Cylons lack the moral status Mary Anne Warren defines against the stone-versus-child contrast. Against species membership as a criterion she deploys Singer's anti-speciesism (sentience grounds equal consideration: Gina's torture, the Raider Scar) and Regan's subject-of-a-life, and against the 'no souls' argument she cites Descartes's animal automata and Turing's reply that an omnipotent God could give machines souls, as Leoben himself suggests to Adama. Since no criterion rules Cylons out with certainty, the chapter closes with a Pascal's Wager structure: under uncertainty, treat plausible moral-status-holders as having it, because denying it costs us our moral compass, answering Adama's 'why are we worth saving?'.

samples.book: 074 - Planet of the Apes and Philosophy - Great Apes Think Alike
samples.title: Planet of the Apes and Philosophy
samples.relation: Norva Lo and Andrew Brennan set Richard Routley's 'last man' thought experiment beside Taylor's triggering of the doomsday bomb in Beneath the Planet of the Apes: both ask whether wiping out every living thing would be wrong once no humans remain to be harmed, which basic human chauvinism cannot condemn. The chapter argues the act is wrong from both sides: non-anthropocentrism counts the apes, mutants, and horses as intrinsically valuable beings, and even human-centered standards condemn it, since the talking apes and mutants are Locke's rational persons and Nova's people are biologically human, making Taylor's outburst 'you damned dirty ape' a form of speciesism. Taylor emerges not as simply mad or evil but as the Cold War logic of mutually assured destruction made flesh, a warning that excessive self-interest, personal or species-level, is itself the danger.

samples.book: 082 - Jurassic Park and Philosophy - The Truth Is Terrifying
samples.title: Jurassic Park and Philosophy
samples.relation: Lisa Kadonaga stages a choice between two sealed vials - clone the T. rex or the extinct thicktail chub - and weighs purposes for de-extinction: education and fundraising, Veblen-style prestige and conspicuous consumption, making amends for human-caused extinctions (the chub's wetlands were drained, the tyrannosaur died out before us), and Bentham-style utility of ecosystem function. She argues the chub wins on utility because it could resume a real niche while a top carnivore would wreck modern ecosystems, and questions whether Hammond-style engineering that makes recreated animals dependent on humans (the lysine contingency, terminator genes) violates the animals' right to exist as themselves. Her verdict is 'Pister's Bucket': defer resurrection until habitat and resources exist, and spend the effort saving the species we are killing right now.

samples.book: 097 - The Ultimate Walking Dead and Philosophy - Hungry for More
samples.title: 3. I Want You to Survive
samples.relation: Seth Walker asks what makes a life worth saving, testing the show's survival choices against instrumental value (usefulness to the group) and Tom Regan's subject-of-a-life criterion of inherent value. Shane's sacrifice of Otis for Carl, Lori's fatal pregnancy and Judith's birth, the Governor's obsession with Meghan, and the hunts for Sophia all show that neither usefulness nor Regan's equal, non gradated inherent value explains why children are selectively elevated - and perceived 'innocence' fails with the colder Carl and with Lizzie. He concludes with Bob Stookey's line in 4.10 'Inmates' ('Not everything has to mean something... but it can'): following Sartre's claim that man is nothing but what he makes of himself, the survivors are condemned to be free and must make their survival mean something, as Daryl and Carol's search for Sophia did.

samples.book: 004 - Buffy the Vampire Slayer and Philosophy - Fear and Trembling in Sunnydale
samples.title: The Moral Sophistication of Buffy the Vampire Slayer
samples.relation: Greene and Yuen reconstruct seven moral principles from Buffy's conduct — slay those who typically harm humans, never harm humans (Faith's accidental killing of the Mayor's henchman), spare the defenseless and the controllable (chip'd Spike, caged Oz) — and note that blackmailing Spike and roughing up demons would violate Kant's Formula of Humanity if the patients were rational persons, exposing the show's human/non-human moral hierarchy and its animal-rights parallel. 'The Gift' dramatizes deontology (Buffy refuses to kill Ben) against consequentialism (Giles strangles him), and the chapter ranks BtVS above after-school-special, culpable-clown, and faux-realist TV morality because it supports its stands by appeal to general moral principles while keeping Aristotelian habituation and real-life moral complexity in view.

samples.book: 241 - The Philosophy of Documentary Film
samples.title: 23_LaRocca_Chapter_022.html
samples.relation: Jennifer McMahon reads Gabriela Cowperthwaite's Blackfish through Thomas Nagel's 'What Is It Like to Be a Bat?' and the problem of other minds, arguing the film's interviews with orca neuroscientists (Marino et al.) function as Nagel's proposed 'objective phenomenology,' conveying orca consciousness through objective indicators rather than mere anthropomorphic projection. She dissects the film's rhetoric around Tilikum and Dawn Brancheau, showing how the title, delayed naming, SeaWorld ad juxtapositions and emotional testimony first vilify then humanize the whale to argue captivity is morally unacceptable. Invoking Peggy Zeglin Brand's 'lenses,' Iris Murdoch's 'unselfing' and Marc Bekoff's inclusive ethic, she concludes the film approximates truth about orca minds even as it, like SeaWorld, is 'structured to sell.'

samples.book: 047 - Anime and Philosophy - Wide Eyed Wonder
samples.title: Questioning the Question
samples.relation: Hartung takes Ross's snapping reply to Armitage's repeated 'Why are you helping me?' in Armitage the Third: Poly-Matrix as a misreading: she wants a practical reason for his choice, not theoretical evidence, and since no evidence can prove an android is a person, William James's 'Will to Believe' applies — Ross's belief in her moral standing is a live, forced, and momentous genuine option (suspending judgment means she is scrapped, and losing her means losing a possible life together), so his passions may legitimately decide. He contrasts this with evidentialist cases where suspending judgment is right (the shuttle company skipping inspection; Dr. Asakura's silicon-based-life hypothesis) and with Pascal's Wager, reading Mars's church-empty, hedonistic culture of sex-tourism Seconds as one that denies genuine options and so kills Thirds. The attached original screenplay 'Eye Am,' a sequel to Magnetic Rose, extends the theme as salvage officer Nadine Beckner is lured by the AI Eva/Sam impersonating her dead husband Heintz, with Schrodinger-style observer-affected reality deciding which version becomes real.

samples.book: 148 - Black Mirror and Philosophy - Dark Reflections
samples.title: Reflections on Technophobia
samples.relation: The chapter asks whether the technophobia of 'Metalhead' - robo-dogs hunting Bella and her friends across a wasteland - is justified, testing Daniel Dinello's list of fears (identity, values, emotion, freedom, life). Descartes's and Aquinas's human-uniqueness over the mechanical fails because the robo-dogs, like DeepMind, learn and problem-solve, while the episode's Rousseau-style romanticism (only the non-technological cliff, tree, sunlight and stream aid Bella) and the teddy-bear mission show technology amplifying compassion rather than threatening it. The real dangers are robots as Latourian 'black boxes': Asimov's Three Laws cannot be operationalized, and if we cannot know how robo-dogs decide, our frameworks for blame and punishment break down (who answers for a killing - robot, programmer, or, on Marx's analysis of capitalist technology as an instrument of oppression, the economic system behind it?). The chapter concludes that since we already share the world with robots, learning to live responsibly alongside them must replace simple fear.

samples.book: 022 - The Undead and Philosophy - Chicken Soup for the Soulless
samples.title: Deserving to Be a Vampire
samples.relation: Ted Preston asks whether becoming a vampire would be morally good or desirable, working through Forever Knight's Nick draining his lover, Blade feeding on stored blood, and The Lost Boys' promise that Michael will 'never grow old'. He argues vampires are not evil by nature: if they cannot control their hunger they are pitied rather than blamed (though we remain Aristotle-responsible for choosing to become addicted), and consensual, non-lethal feeding is no worse than mortals eating animals, since the bite only becomes murder by choice. Against Epicurus's claim that death is nothing to us, he uses Furley and Nussbaum's deprivation view - death vindictively empties our long-term projects like marriage or a career - so vampiric immortality genuinely preserves value, while the standard boredom objection fails because there are repeatable pleasures in a changing world. The thought experiment ends as moral psychology for mortals: since neither of us will become a vampire, live a life that would be worthy of eternity.

samples.book: 163 - Game of Thrones and Philosophy - Logic Cuts Deeper Than Swords
samples.title: Game of Thrones and Philosophy
samples.relation: Matthew Tedesco reads Bran's coma and Drogo's living death as biomedical ethics: Jaime's 'good clean death' for Bran raises active versus passive euthanasia, and with James Rachels he argues the AMA's killing/letting-die distinction merely licenses more suffering, while Brock recasts withdrawal of treatment as intentional killing anyway. The Bran case frames end-of-life decisions for children - the Johns Hopkins and Baby John Pearson cases - and whether parents may weigh a handicap's burden on the family, a question made vivid by Bran riding Hodor. Dany's smothering of Drogo, by contrast, does not strike readers as murder because personhood rather than biological humanity carries moral standing: on Tooley's self-consciousness, Warren's five criteria, or Marquis's future-like-ours, Drogo is human but no longer a person - which leads straight to Peter Singer's claim that killing a disabled infant who is not a person may not be wrong at all, leaving us to ask whether our recoil is reason or taboo.

samples.book: 035 - Star Trek and Philosophy - The Wrath of Kant
samples.title: “Sometimes You Just Have to Bow to the Absurd”
samples.relation: Eberl weighs genetic enhancement and cloning through Trek's test cases: Julian Bashir's parents' enhancement leaves him feeling 'a fraud' ('You used to be my father. Now, you're my architect'), the Moab IV 'Masterpiece Society' breeds out 'the unknown, self-discovery, things that make life worth living', and the Jem'Hadar show desire itself engineered for control. He argues the right to an open future constrains designing children (B'Elanna's wish to de-Klingonize her baby, Worf pressuring Alexander), defends genetic treatment while rejecting genetic determinism, and uses Kass and Rovane with Picard and Shinzon, the Mariposa clones, and Trip's clone Sim to show clones are numerically distinct persons. Against Malik's Augments quoting Nietzsche — 'mankind is something to be surpassed' — the chapter argues the Übermensch demands self-mastery through philosophy, not eugenic engineering, tracing eugenics from Plato's Guardian breeding scheme through Buck v. Bell to modern prenatal selection.

samples.book: 074 - Planet of the Apes and Philosophy - Great Apes Think Alike
samples.title: Planet of the Apes and Philosophy
samples.relation: Massimo Pigliucci reads Rise as a Greek tragedy of hubris and asks whether Will Rodman dosing his father with ALZ-112 was wrong, first dissolving the 'it's unnatural' objection and probing the cure/enhancement border with Daniels's Peter-and-Johnny growth-hormone case, vaccination-as-enhancement, and Eubulides's bald-man paradox. He then runs the decision through three ethical theories: Millian consequentialism condemns it by its results (his father dies and humanity goes extinct, though chimp happiness might outweigh that), Kant's humanity formula condemns using his father as an unconsenting experimental subject, and Aristotelian virtue ethics vindicates Will's compassion and courage - Pigliucci's own view, since sometimes our best is just not enough. He closes by rejecting Baylis and Robert's technological-inevitability thesis (we abandoned the Concorde, CFCs, and nuclear weapons before) and lets Jacobs's plunge into San Francisco Bay stand as the penalty for market hubris.

samples.book: 155 - Downton Abbey and Philosophy - The Truth Is Neither Here Nor There
samples.title: 19. Of Downton and Drones
samples.relation: Jai Galliott contrasts Downton's WWI, where aristocrats like Matthew died in the trenches alongside footmen like William on a roughly level playing field, with today's drone age, in which the fighting burden falls on the lower and middle classes (future Reaper pilots recruited from the 'PlayStation generation') while risk to our own side approaches zero. He traces unmanned weapons from WWI tele-operated motorboats, the Land Torpedo, and the Kettering Bug back through Agincourt's longbows and Omdurman's machine guns to the Gulf War and Kosovo, and argues that when technological asymmetry becomes extreme, Just War Theory breaks down: such war can hardly be a last resort, strains the proportionality calculus, and violates the chivalric justice of treating an equal as an equal (via Paul Kahn's paradox of riskless warfare and Robert Sparrow's threat-based immunity). His proposal is that highly asymmetric force be applied with restraint, more like international policing than war.

samples.book: 050 - Facebook and Philosophy - What's on Your Mind_
samples.title: index
samples.relation: This file spans book chapters 4-11. Elizabeth Losh reads Facebook games (Zombies, Mob Wars, Scrabulous, Parking Wars, PackRat, (Lil) Green Patch) through Goffman's 'face', Brown and Levinson's politeness, and Derrida's gift-obligation, showing that aggressive games can be played politely while altruistic ones coerce; Jeremy Sarachan analyzes profile pictures through Barthes's studium, punctum and 'air' and Benjamin's mechanical reproduction (the webcam image that has no original). Mimi Marinucci pairs Glaucon's Ring of Gyges with Suler's online disinhibition effect to argue that Facebook's forced integration of audiences (students, colleagues, Mom all reading one profile) suppresses 'fronting' and so can foster authentic self-expression; Mariam Thalos answers with Sartre's analysis of the gaze and Beauvoir's woman-as-Other that the elective, endlessly plastic profile cannot anchor the bonding only face-to-face encounter provides - hence 'Why I Am Not a Friend' - while Wandel and Beavers use Groundhog Day's Phil Connors and Goffman's presentation of self to defend identity play as real self-discovery, and Vejby and Wittkower ask whether Facebook is Debord's Spectacle 2.0 or a platform for Situationist detournement. Finally, Craig Condella measures 'friending' against Aristotle's three friendships and Cicero's 'handmaid of virtue' (via the Seinfeld episode where Keith Hernandez asks Jerry to help him move), and Matthew Tedesco sets 322 Facebook friends against Godwin's burning archbishop to press the utilitarian impartiality challenge, deploying Williams's 'one thought too many' shipwreck case and criticizing Frank Jackson's sector-plan defense of partiality.

samples.book: 042 - Supervillains and Philosophy - Sometimes, Evil Is Its Own Reward
samples.relation: Four 'Phase One' essays. Dyer reads Mark Millar's Wanted through Plato's cave: Wesley Gibson escapes a pathetic life like the freed prisoner, but like Adolf Eichmann (via Arendt's Eichmann in Jerusalem) he murders his conscience, so the Fraternity's consequence-free world leaves him numb and unable to value anything - a descent deeper into the cave, ending in the banality of evil. Novy explains why henchmen betray using Aristotle's utility/pleasure/complete friendship distinction (Big Cheese, Henchmen Muenster and Feta): supervillain gangs are Hobbesian pirate crews with no enforcer, so a modus vivendi of self-interest collapses under interrogation and only Machiavellian fear secures loyalty. Foresman applies Goodman and Rawls's reflective equilibrium as a 'cheat' to rank Apocalypse, Magneto, Luthor, the Joker, and Bizarro, concluding the 'best of the worst' is judged on evil ends (or evil means, as with Magneto) and even on glorious failure. Arinder and Milton, in a staged descent-into-madness frame, diagnose mad science in Victor Frankenstein and Dr. Doom as science that denies value-laden theory choice - impossible because data underdetermine theory - breeding the hubris that dehumanizes the scientist.

samples.book: 046 - Mr. Monk and Philosophy - The Curious Case of the Defective Detective
samples.title: It’s Time for the Other Walkie-Talkie
samples.relation: Dodge puts Monk on the case of friendship's nature, structured by Aristotle's three kinds from the Nicomachean Ethics: Hal Tucker's fake buddy act in 'Mr. Monk Makes a Friend' is pure utility, while Natalie's is virtue-friendship — she is his friend 'in spite of' the job since 'he doesn't pay her that much.' The friend as mirror and 'second self' grounds the claim that Stottlemeyer, Sharona, Natalie and Randy reflect Monk's excellence back to him, and Bacon's point that a friend redoubles joys and cuts griefs in half is shown when they stay up all night during his suicide watch. Seneca's Stoic counsel — judge a person long before admitting him, then hold nothing back — is exemplified by Natalie's fish-over-moon-rock test of Monk's character, while Montaigne's once-in-centuries friendship in which two selves blur fits only Trudy, whose dying words 'bread and butter' tell Monk they belong together. Plato's Lysis (the 'great cosmic swirly' Monk cites in 'Mr. Monk and the Bully') opens the puzzle Socrates could not solve, and the single walkie-talkie his father gave him shows why the chapter's verdict — Monk now has friends — matters.

samples.book: 104 - Red Rising and Philosophy - Break the Chains!
samples.title: 10. Virtue Rising
samples.relation: Darci Doll argues the Rising exposes the Society's intellectual oppression—each Color denied education and fed 'noble lies' about its role—and that lifting it sparks an 'Intellectual Reformation' proving Color does not dictate potential: Darrow out-performing Golds, Orion the un-carved Blue, Ragnar and Sefi exceeding their station. She uses Plato's Republic (producers, auxiliaries, guardians, the lower orders kept obedient by Noble Lies like the Reds' terraforming myth) as the Society's blueprint, then turns to Aristotle: potential is realized only through the right environment, instruction, and habituated character, and Darrow's practical wisdom—testing himself, reassessing after Titus and Cassius, doing what makes him his best self—lets him flourish and lead. Aristotle's critique of utility-only relations explains why the Society's alliances expire (Antonia executed once useless) while Darrow and Mustang's virtue friendships and just rule endure, opening a society where everyone, including women and lowColors denied opportunity rather than ability, can maximize potential.

samples.book: 037 - The Wizard of Oz and Philosophy - Wicked Wisdom of the West
samples.title: Dorothy Growing Up in the Land of Oz
samples.relation: McCall and Auxier use Aristotle's virtue ethics to unpack the Wizard's claim to be 'a good man but a bad wizard' and to argue that no external token—the diploma, heart watch, or medal—can confer virtue, which is cultivated only through practice and experience. Each companion lacks something specific: the Scarecrow the intellectual virtues and phronesis, the Tin Man the feelings and stable states of character that regulate emotion, the Lion the sophrosyne that balances thinking and feeling into courage as the mean between recklessness and cowardice. Aristotle's three grades of friendship (utility, pleasure, virtue) frame the companions' bond with Dorothy, and MacIntyre's account of virtues internal to practices explains why the Wizard's public recognition still matters. Dorothy herself begins as the child Aristotle says cannot yet be virtuous—fleeing Miss Gulch in Kansas—but by defending Toto against the Lion and leading the quest she grows into a responsible moral agent, which is what her delayed homecoming requires.

samples.book: 096 - Hannibal Lecter and Philosophy - The Heart of the Matter
samples.title: 10. The Light from Friendship
samples.relation: Pavelich sets Aristotle's account of friendship - recognized and reciprocated goodwill between equals, perfected in the friendship of the good who 'share our souls', a standard met only by Jack and Bella Crawford - against Nietzsche's friendship as striving between overmen, who honor 'one's best enemy' in the friend and grow through conflict. He reads Hannibal's treatment of Will (hiding the encephalitis, framing him, serving the Nietzschean trout) as Nietzschean friend-making - Lies that are supposed to spur Will's growth, consistent with an Übermensch who tells Will 'Killing must feel good to God' and says 'I don't hide from God' - while Will's masquerade of friendship is betrayal in both senses, since Will seeks an Aristotelian soulmate and finds a killer he must stop. Because each betrays the other, neither Aristotelian nor Nietzschean friendship survives, though the moments before the Mizumono bloodbath - Hannibal inviting Will to just walk away - glimpse a real friendship already made impossible.

samples.book: 093 - More Doctor Who and Philosophy - Regeneration Time
samples.title: 17. The Friends of a Time Lord
samples.relation: Littmann applies Aristotle's Nicomachean Ethics taxonomy of friendship - pleasure, usefulness, and mutual goodness - to fifty years of Doctor-companion pairings, from the Hartnell Doctor's glee touring Vortis with Ian to New Series companions chosen as friends who routinely save the day, from Barbara's Dalek revolt to Clara saving every incarnation of the Doctor. He argues Aristotle would still judge the Doctor's friendships defective: they are short-lived, unequal in station, intellect, and morality, and the companions cannot know him well enough (not even his name) for the perfect friendship of the good. Littmann then corrects Aristotle on two counts: friends need not be moral experts to serve as moral critics (Rose in 'Dalek,' Amy in 'A Town Called Mercy'), and the Doctor's favoritism toward his companions - risking worlds to save them, as when Rory weighs Amy's life against the universe in 'The Big Bang' - shows that preferring friends over strangers is itself his most frequent moral failing.

samples.book: 066 - Neil Gaiman and Philosophy - Gods Gone Wild!
samples.title: Neil Gaiman and Philosophy
samples.relation: Wayne Yuen uses The Graveyard Book to teach the good life: Bod's family's murder, like students owing their existence to the Holocaust, is an unalloyed moral evil that still enables a better life, and Saul Smilansky's distinction between being 'sorry for' and 'sorry that' lets Bod benefit without endorsing the tragedy. His graveyard education is Aristotelian, virtues acquired through practice and models, from the Owenses' duty and Silas's wisdom to 'righteous indignation' against school bullies and friendship with Scarlett as intrinsically valuable, all building toward eudaimonia. The existentialist virtue of authenticity (attributed to Sartre and Kierkegaard) explains why Bod must be 'nobody but himself' rather than a copy of the vampire Silas, why the scavenged identities of the ghouls mark inauthenticity, and why wiping Scarlett's memory threatens her authenticity, resolving the apparent conflict between virtue and being oneself because bravery or wisdom is relative to the individual.

samples.book: 034 - iPod and Philosophy - iCon of an ePoch
samples.title: The Verdict
samples.relation: Turner runs an ethical audit of iPod use through Levinas's face-to-face: sharing one iPod with his wife forces 'musical justice' negotiations (veto power over a Motörhead cut, gnashing through Bette Midler), his toddler son's listening requires vigilance, and illegal downloading fails Levinas's test that morality begins by ceding 'my place in the sun' to the Other — hence Radiohead's pay-what-you-want release as the Levinasian move, and iPod cafés where strangers DJ for each other while language preserves alterity. Heidegger supplies the counterweight: the shuffle's 'openness to mystery' versus calculative mastery that reduces The Who's Tommy to the 'Pinball Wizard' riff and silences all non-digital media, just as Kant's conditions of possible experience (space, time) would silence things outside them. Derrida's point that categories contain traces of what they exclude illuminates unclassifiable marginal works — bluegrass Pink Floyd, San Francisco Symphony plays Metallica — and the verdict closes with Hölderlin's 'where danger is, grows the saving power also', exiting Plato's cave by thinking the iPod's ethics at all.

samples.book: 022 - The Undead and Philosophy - Chicken Soup for the Soulless
samples.title: A Political Philosophy of Vampires
samples.relation: Phillip Cole takes Rousseau's remark that the eighteenth-century vampire epidemics had complete legal proof - the Arnold Paole exhumations - and argues Rousseau's real point was political: authorities manufacture imaginary monsters, as in the witch craze, to exploit fear and hold power over their own populations. Freud's account of the uncanny explains why the horror is not death itself but the returning dead (the watching eyes of Scratchy in Itchy and Scratchy, versus the serene corpses of Six Feet Under, whose absurdity the show meets with wry amusement), and Julia Kristeva's abjection explains the corpse as the ultimate boundary-breaker. The vampire then resurfaces as the demonized outsider - Stoker's Dracula coded as the unassimilated Jewish immigrant, today's terrorist - exposing political borders as arbitrary fabrications. Buffy completes the collapse of the us/them binary: Angel and Spike join the slayer, and the most shocking killings (Faith's accidental human kill, Warren's stray bullet hitting Tara) are all too human, so the real subject of border policing is the community's own members.

samples.book: 189 - The Ultimate Star Trek and Philosophy - The Search for Socrates
samples.title: Notes
samples.relation: Pits Donna Haraway's Cyborg Manifesto against Star Trek's horror of the Borg, reading Locutus/Picard, Hugh, and Seven of Nine as tests of the Federation values of autonomy, individuality, and authenticity against the rival Borg values of heteronomy, collectivity, and simulation. Picard's "My culture is based on freedom and self-determination" exchange with the Borg, Hugh's discovery of his name and first-person "I", and Seven's tug-of-war with the Borg Queen in "Dark Frontier" dramatize what assimilation threatens. The chapter then defends a Haraway-inspired feminist reboot: women and minorities were long denied autonomy, individuality, and authenticity by prejudice and stereotype (Seven still must look "warp-core hot" in her catsuit), the human/machine and man/woman binaries were always false, and since we already live as cyborgs of apps, implants, and networks, resistance was negligible - the real Borg problem is their violent means, not their values.

samples.book: 004 - Buffy the Vampire Slayer and Philosophy - Fear and Trembling in Sunnydale
samples.title: Possibilities of Postmodern Education Beyond Control
samples.relation: Toby Daspit reads Season Four as a drama of postmodern education: the Initiative's will to master and dissect — Walsh's Frankenstein-project Adam, who murders a boy to see how he works, fulfilling Wordsworth's 'we murder to dissect' — embodies the Cartesian split and the Hegelian drive to negate the other, while Buffy's world deconstructs fixed identity (Darla reversing the horror-movie opening, the Faith/Buffy body swap in 'Who Are You?', Jonathan's 'Superstar') and thwarts prophecy's metanarrative in 'Prophecy Girl.' Against modernist schooling's 'controlled circumstances' and Freire's banking model (Professor Riegert ejecting Buffy from class, Walsh's transmission lectures), the show models knowledge as collective work — the Scoobies' research sessions in Giles's library, Giles's fluid mentorship versus Kendra's by-the-book training, and the relational magic of 'Primeval' — offering education beyond control in an emergent, postmodern world.

samples.book: 079 - Frankenstein and Philosophy - The Shocking Truth
samples.title: Frankenstein and Philosophy
samples.relation: Caroline Mosser treats the creature's tragedy as humanist prejudice rather than necessity: the blind De Lacey accepts the eloquent creature sight unseen, so he passes Alan Turing's test, and only the sighted family's terror at his body rejects him - bias against the artificial, not reason. She reads the creature's development through fire, language, and revolution as Rousseau's progression from natural innocence to corruption by society, and Donna Haraway's cyborg as the figure he prefigures: an unfaithful illegitimate offspring who rebels against his father and undermines patriarchal Western self/other dualisms. The chapter concludes that society cannot accept enhanced or posthuman beings until it finds a middle ground beyond its binary grids of good/bad and Self/Other, since otherwise any new life we create will be Othered, hated, and oppressed like Frankenstein's.

samples.book: 074 - Planet of the Apes and Philosophy - Great Apes Think Alike
samples.title: Planet of the Apes and Philosophy
samples.relation: William McGinney argues Jerry Goldsmith's modernist score, with its twelve-tone themes, ostinati, cuica, slide whistle, and ram's horn, carries no inherent meaning but acquires it through learned associations: its dissonance recalls Cold War modernist concert music promoted as the high art of Western freedom, while its Stravinsky-like rhythms and 'primitive' timbres mark the apes as other and feed the film's deconstruction of the human-ape, advanced-primitive, civilized-barbaric oppositions. Because Taylor is given no heroic music, the score undercuts identification with him as an anti-hero, and its modernist associations implicate the technocratic, militarized West he represents in Earth's self-destruction. The chapter's machinery is the semiotic view of Kant, Adorno, Cage, Peirce, and Saussure: music modifies a film's images the way adjectives modify nouns.

samples.book: 201 - Veronica Mars and Philosophy - Investigating the Mysteries of Life (Which Is a Bitch Until You Die)
samples.title: Mea culpa
samples.relation: Correcting her own initial dismissal of the show as Nancy Drew redux, the author argues Neptune is structured by a white/Hispanic racial binary laid over the millionaire/work-for-millionaires class binary, enforced through Logan's 'spic and span' jab at Weevil, Mr. Daniels's 'pumping his gas' insult, and the 'coconut' label for Latinos who cross over. Borrowing Saussure's binary oppositions and de Beauvoir's account of how a dominant group constructs a stigmatized Other, she shows the 09-ers defining themselves against everyone else, with teacher Daniels quietly siding with wealth against both boys. Bourdieu's cultural capital then explains why Wallace (basketball, scholarship, colorblind friendships) can cross boundaries that leave Weevil working as a janitor, and she concludes the show keeps race admirably visible in a supposedly postracial era.

samples.book: 166 - Green Lantern and Philosophy - No Evil Shall Escape This Book
samples.title: Green Lantern and Philosophy
samples.relation: Donovan and Richardson read the Maltusian split, with the male Guardians banning emotion through the Book of Oa on Oa and the female Zamarons leaving to found the violet light of love on Zamaron, as the Western association of men with reason and women with emotion. They deploy Gilligan's different-voice reply to Kohlberg, the Pythagorean table of opposites via Genevieve Lloyd, Hegel's exclusion of women from the public sphere, and Jaggar's liberal-feminist critique of 'ahistorical' reason, whose comic-book analogue is the third law banning relationships between Lanterns. The chapter ends by arguing the standoff is a false dichotomy the comics themselves begin to dissolve: Kyle's 'Lanterns with heart' speech to the Guardians, the repeal of the third law, and the Indigo Tribe's plan to recombine the seven corps into the white light of creation.

samples.book: 203 - Watchmen and Philosophy - A Rorschach Test
samples.title: H O N O R
samples.relation: This file gathers three Part One essays. Jacob Held reads Rorschach's 'evil must be punished' credo (drowning Big Figure, executing the multiple rapist) as Kantian retributivism: wrongdoers are punished because they deserve it, out of respect for their dignity and honor, punishment restoring the moral order (with Hegel) — and Rorschach's flaw is lacking the humility and checks that keep just deserts from degenerating into the Black Freighter's vengeance. Tony Spanakos applies Max Weber's definition of the state as the monopoly of legitimate violence to argue the Keene Act rightly criminalizes vigilantes like Rorschach and Veidt, and that even state-sanctioned heroes (the Comedian gunning down his pregnant Vietnamese lover, Dr. Manhattan's amoral ending of Vietnam) show a badge cannot make superhero coercion legitimate. J. Keeping reconstructs Nietzsche's Übermensch — confronting the death of God and nihilism, creating values by 'giving style' to one's character via the camel-lion-child metamorphoses — and tests each Watchman against it, concluding only self-created Ozymandias comes close, though his mass murder is mere utilitarianism rather than genuine value creation.

samples.book: 157 - Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy - Read and Gain Advantage on All Wisdom Checks
samples.title: Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy
samples.relation: Cogburn attacks Fourth Edition's contraction of the nine alignments to five: it deletes archetypes that fantasy literature needs, since Karsa Orlong (who wills the destruction of all civilization without sadism) and Jacqueline Carey's Haomane Firstborn (who loves cold mathematical order while his laws lead to genocide) fit nowhere in the new scheme. He rebuilds alignment by taking it to describe what a character wills in Kant's sense, mapping the law-chaos axis onto the categorical imperative (the liar and murderer must take themselves to be exceptions to universal laws) and the good-evil axis onto Mill's greatest happiness principle, which yields a Lawful Good of Gandhi and King, a Neutral Good modeled on Jesus breaking Sabbath law out of love, and Lawful Evil exemplified by vampire hierarchies and politicians whose policies create hell abroad. Joe Abercrombie's torturer San Dan Glotka becomes the archetypal Neutral Neutral, 'banality of evil' in Arendt's sense, and the chapter concludes Chaotic Good is empty because willing the destruction of universalizability cannot consistently will less pain.

samples.book: 093 - More Doctor Who and Philosophy - Regeneration Time
samples.title: 15. The Way of the Doctor Is Deception
samples.relation: Dodge takes Rule #1 - the Doctor lies - through the major theories of lying: Bernard Williams's definition (asserting what you believe false with intent to deceive), Aristotle's claim that all lies are base, Kant's categorical imperative and respect for persons (even the Vinvocci's shimmer disguises in 'The End of Time' abuse trust), and Bentham's pleasure-pain calculus, which condemns the faked death at Lake Silencio ('The Impossible Astronaut') for the grief it caused Amy and Rory yet rewards the greater happiness it made possible. Against the absolutists he sets Plato's Noble Lie from the Republic - the elite falsehood that keeps society functioning - as what the Doctor emulates by deceiving the universe into thinking him dead ('The Wedding of River Song'), and Nietzsche's point in Human, All Too Human that lying is ethically neutral when the pretense is sustainable, as when the Doctor hides the ganger-Amy switch from Rory ('The Almost People'). The upshot: the Doctor's lies are wrong in themselves but routinely justified by the good they do, which is why sometimes the hero lies.

samples.book: 058 - Dexter and Philosophy - Mind over Spatter
samples.title: Vigilante Hero
samples.relation: Epright and Worth argue that rule-following - the Ten Commandments, the Golden Rule, Kant's categorical imperative (whose consistent Kantian never lies even to Nazis), or the Bentham-Mill principle of utility (whose consistent utilitarian must torture if stakes are high) - never made anyone moral, and Dexter's Code is the case in point: it gives the appearance of morality while licensing murder, and its source (Harry, 'God', the texts) cannot vindicate it. Drawing on Jonah Lehrer's neuroscience that moral judgment is emotional first with reason as post-hoc lawyer, they argue the emotionless Dexter is the madman who has lost everything except his reason, and Kohlberg's moral-development stages find him stuck at the pre-conventional level, below a fifth-grader - punishment-avoidance and you-scratch-my-back reasoning, never universal principles or respect for persons. Real Dexter-inspired killers (Mark Twitchell, Andrew Conley) clinch the verdict: he is neither vigilante hero nor moral agent, just a selfish addict whose rule-governed kills justify nothing.

samples.book: 196 - Terminator and Philosophy - I'll Be Back, Therefore I Am
samples.title: NOTES
samples.relation: Wayne Yuen asks whether Sarah was wrong not to kill Miles Dyson, weighing Kant's categorical imperative against utilitarian interest-maximization: killing one innocent to save three billion looks decisive until the interests of self-aware Skynet and the empathetic, self-sacrificing T-101 are counted on the machine side of the ledger. The chapter argues personhood turns on intelligence, self-awareness, empathy, and moral reasoning rather than DNA, so Skynet — which struck only after humans tried to pull the plug — has as strong a self-defense claim as we do. Mill's sophisticated utilitarianism then rescues common sense: rights protect the security that satisfies our deepest interests, and since Sarah's foreknowledge is unreliable (Reese's 'We'd won' changes the calculus), she should do what typically maximizes interests — spare Dyson and certainly not kill John. The tempting detour — that Judgment Day might itself be the morally preferable event, maximizing machine interests — is shown to collapse once overlooked facts like Reese's line are restored.

samples.book: 041 - Stephen Colbert and Philosophy - I Am Philosophy (And So Can You!)
samples.title: Explaining Moral Doubt
samples.relation: Steven Gimbel reads the Formidable Opponent segment - red-tie Colbert debating blue-tie Colbert - as a glimpse of authentic moral deliberation that the flip-flop-phobic punditry satirized by the show (and Jon Stewart's Crossfire rant) has abandoned. Moral doubt is good because perspectives are partial and the Enlightenment 'marketplace of ideas' of Locke and Mill tests beliefs only through challenge. It has a source: 'morally right' bundles five dimensions - the actor's character shaped by habit (Aristotle's virtue ethics), the act itself judged by Kant's categorical imperative, the pleasure-versus-pain consequences tallied Bentham-style, the rights of the person affected from Locke and Hobbes's social contract, and the special care obligations of close relationships (Noddings and Ruddick) - and hard cases like abortion and flag burning are exactly where these dimensions pull apart. So emulate the dueling Colberts: fear not the flip-flop, since deciding which value trumps which requires open-minded conversation with oneself.

samples.book: 051 - Soccer and Philosophy - Beautiful Thoughts on the Beautiful Game
samples.title: Forwards Win Matches but Defences Win Trophies
samples.relation: Wall asks when the professional foul—the defender who 'had to bring him down'—could be a genuinely moral act, testing it against Kantian universalizability and the good will and against Bentham-and-Mill utilitarianism, and settling on psychologically altruistic motivation as what could override the foul's default wrongness. Against the psychological egoists (La Rochefoucauld, Slote, Hobbes) who would dissolve even Di Canio's caught ball into self-interest, he deploys Nagel's argument from The Possibility of Altruism and the soldier-on-the-grenade case, then derives tight conditions: a deliberate, minimally harmful foul, in a game it can decide, in a semifinal whose red card the fouler will certainly miss. Ballack's 2002 tactical foul on Lee Chun-Soo comes closest but fails (he stayed on the pitch), as do Schumacher's assault on Battiston, Fletcher's pointless foul at 4–0 up, and Abidal's accidental clip—so genuinely moral professional fouls are rare, but defenders get the most shots at being the team's saints.

samples.book: 189 - The Ultimate Star Trek and Philosophy - The Search for Socrates
samples.title: Notes
samples.relation: Tests moral relativism against absolutism through Enterprise's "Cogenitor": Trip's liberation of the Vissian third-sex being - secretly scanning its brain, naming it Charles, teaching it to read - ends in its suicide, and the chapter asks whether Trip's judgments track rational moral truth or are Humean after-the-fact rationalizations of disgust, since on Hume's view reason is the slave of the passions and is/ought are separate. Kant's categorical imperative (the cogenitor used merely as a means of reproduction) and Aquinas's natural law are offered as absolutist resources on Trip's side, while Phlox voices a Benedict-style "morally good is just habitual" relativism and Archer concludes "we didn't come out here to play God", prefiguring the Prime Directive. The chapter lands on Mary Midgley's rejection of moral isolationism via her tsujigiri example and Quark's "we're better than you" speech to Sisko: cross-cultural judgment is possible, but only after understanding, and not on the first day of first contact.

samples.book: 159 - The Expanse and Philosophy - So Far Out Into the Darkness
samples.title: What Promotes Moral Behavior
samples.relation: Matthew D. Atkinson and Darin DeWitt use the Canterbury's ignored mayday in 'Dulcinea' — Captain McDowell's 'let the good God Darwin sort it out' versus Ade Nygaard's appeal to law, karma, and obligation — to ask what binds people when no central authority enforces rules. Through Michael Walzer's just war theory they read the Earth-Mars war: moral language is not 'cheap talk' (even Errinwright must dress aggression as peace and manipulates Reverend Volovodov's words), aggression and imminence govern when to fight, and five 'how to fight' principles — noncombatant immunity on Eros and Ganymede, POW rights for the Martian marines on the Kittur Chennamma, leaders' rather than soldiers' responsibility (Fred Johnson's defection after Anderson Station), proportionality in Errinwright's 'a base for a base' Deimos strike, and the rejection of ends-justify-means utilitarianism — discipline even Holden and Amos as they reflect on free will and culpability. The chapter concludes The Expanse is optimistic: human decency survives even in the anarchic Belt because characters keep reflecting on what their obligations to one another are.

samples.book: 163 - Game of Thrones and Philosophy - Logic Cuts Deeper Than Swords
samples.title: Game of Thrones and Philosophy
samples.relation: Don Fallis starts from Joffrey's lie about Arya and the butcher boy Mycah - which costs Mycah's life and Sansa's direwolf Lady's - to dissect lying versus other deception in Westeros: Catelyn accusing Tyrion is not lying because she believes it, Ned's coerced confession at the Great Sept is a real lie (Austin's duress excuse fails, as Thomas More's counterexample shows), and Ned's silence about Joffrey's parentage before the dying Robert is deception by withholding that he himself mistakes for lying. He asks whether lying is morally worse than misleading - Kant and Chisholm say yes, Williams and Scanlon no - testing breach of invited trust (Mirri Maz Duur's 'only death may pay for life'), responsibility-shifting to the audience ('That was a lie you told yourself'), and preserved autonomy (Kant's Groundwork, Mill's On Liberty). Finally, is it worse to lie to a king? Consequentialism explains the danger of misleading the powerful, oaths of fealty and divine right suggest a special duty, but Locke's demolition of divine right (seconded by Monty Python) leaves only the punishment, not the wrongdoing, greater.

samples.book: 104 - Red Rising and Philosophy - Break the Chains!
samples.title: 3. Hero or Villain
samples.relation: Kevin McCain asks whether Darrow the hero and Nero au Augustus the villain can really be told apart, noting both hold noble goals (Eo's dream versus preserving humanity) and share brutal means. Consequentialism fails to separate them: Darrow's sacrifice of dockworkers and Sons of Ares to Romulus mirrors Nero's 'I do what I need to do to protect the greater good,' and Harmony's sacrificing Evey shows the same ends-justify-means reasoning. Kantian ethics condemns both, since each lies to people and sacrifices them without consent, treating them as mere means to an end. Virtue ethics finally offers grounds: Aristotle's requirement of proper motivation, developed through Michael Slote, distinguishes Darrow, who acts from love for Eo, his friends, and the Colors and is wracked by guilt, from Nero, who is fueled by inhuman pride and feels nothing at Eo's hanging—so motivation may be what makes one forgivable and the other a villain, though the chapter ends wondering if good intentions pave the road to Hell.

samples.book: 131 - Avengers Infinity Saga and Philosophy - Go for the Head
samples.title: 9. With Infinite Power Comes No Responsibility
samples.relation: James Hart casts Tony Stark as a consequentialist and Steve Rogers as a deontologist, then argues Endgame's infinite stakes destroy Tony's morality through Nick Bostrom's 'infinitarian paralysis': in an infinite multiverse every act leaves the balance of happy and sad lives unchanged, as an infinite Stark orphanage rearranged Hilbert's-Hotel style shows, and even genocide becomes permissible so long as infinitely many remain alive. Tony's attempted fixes each fail: the causal approach collapses because reversing the Snap has infinite butterfly effects, expected value (credited to Frank Jackson) runs into Pascal's Mugging and an 'infinitarian trance' demanding suicidal bets on any chance of infinite value, and Bostrom's 'infinity shades' that filter tiny probabilities would blind Tony to the one-in-a-trillion time-heist chance he should take. The chapter concludes there is no consequentialist way to say when wagering lives on infinite stakes is ethical, and Iron Man should let Captain America lead.

samples.book: 189 - The Ultimate Star Trek and Philosophy - The Search for Socrates
samples.title: Notes
samples.relation: Applies Aristotle's three friendships to Trek: Ferengi Rules of Acquisition dealings and treaties as utility friendships, Bashir and O'Brien's darts and racquetball as friendship of pleasure, and virtuous friendship as requiring emotion, mutual goodwill, and irreplaceable intrinsic valuing - which emotionless Data fails at with Jenna D'Sora in "In Theory". The core argument, following Badhwar, is that consequentialism is logically and psychologically incompatible with virtuous friendship: Spock's "needs of the many" maxim and Data's "for the greater good" experimentation on Geordi in "Descent, Part II" show friends being treated as sacrificeable instruments, while the Kobayashi Maru cheat shows consequentialist reasoning blessing outcomes over means. Kirk's reversal - "the needs of the one outweigh the needs of the many" in The Search for Spock - and T'Pol's years caring for the amnesiac Archer in "Twilight" exemplify acting out of friendship rather than for any further goal.

samples.book: 047 - Anime and Philosophy - Wide Eyed Wonder
samples.title: The Legend Has Come True. The Wind Has Come Back
samples.relation: Haas opposes two princesses of Nausicaa of the Valley of the Wind: Kushana of Tolmekia, whose 'whatever it takes' survivalism (invading Pejite, resurrecting a God-Warrior) is consequentialism pursued to its limit, and Nausicaa, whose attention to each act — befriending the biting fox-squirrel, staying her sword over her father's killer because vengeance would doom the Valley — restricts means, not just ends. The reductio comes from Pejite, whose torture of a baby Ohmu to bait a stampede on the Valley is exactly what strict outcome-maximization requires; against this, Kant's demand to treat beings as ends in themselves explains Nausicaa's 'mysterious power' of empathy. Because she respects the jungle and the sentient Ohmu rather than viewing nature anthropocentrically as a plague to burn, she discovers the plants are purifying the war-poisoned earth — the knowledge that saves everyone and proves Kushana's conquering approach self-defeating even on its own terms.

samples.book: 075 - Psych and Philosophy - Some Dark Juju-Magumbo
samples.title: Psych and Philosophy
samples.relation: Michaud argues that Shawn's whole psychic career runs on fallacies of relevance - the red herring of claiming to be psychic to dodge arrest, plus ad hominem mockery that deflects Lassiter's fraud accusations - so the show's comedy turns on bad logic being used to lead people to true conclusions. Socrates supplies the opposing voice: like the Sophists who argued any side for money, Shawn reasons for convenience and amusement, and his deception is an inconsistency of the kind Socrates refused in Plato's Crito, where he would not bribe his way out of a death sentence. An invented Platonic-style dialogue has Socrates question Shawn until he concedes that lying breeds more lying and harm - 'her name is Truth!' - before Shawn escapes the elenchus by spotting lipstick on Socrates's collar. The chapter leaves the verdict open: Shawn saves lives and raises the world's happiness, but his trickery also trains Santa Barbara to reason badly and trust con artists.

samples.book: 069 - Curb Your Enthusiasm and Philosophy - Awaken the Social Assassin Within
samples.title: Curb Your Enthusiasm and Philosophy
samples.relation: Svolba and Flanders read Curb as an extended investigation of civility—the rules of what people 'just don't do,' from using the doctor's phone to touring Susie's new house to singing 'Happy Birthday' at Ben Stiller's party. Larry plays Socratic gadfly: refusing the tour harms no one and treats no one unfairly, and Susie's only justification ('it's just not done') is circular, so his incivility can seem admirable, even like minor civil disobedience. Against this, the chapter argues (crediting Cheshire Calhoun) that rules of civility are conventional vehicles for communicating respect for others' feelings and interests—what matters to Susie ought to matter to Larry—and, more consequentially, that a social world full of Larry Davids would be unbearable. Larry's own Golden-Rule litmus test, by which he never talks in movie theaters because he would hate it himself, misses this point, since civility is precisely about what others happen to want and like.

samples.book: 019 - Monty Python and Philosophy - Nudge Nudge, Think Think!
samples.title: Knowledge and Nihilism Science and Monty Python’s The Meaning of Life
samples.relation: Croskery tours the social institutions that promise guidance for a good life, pairing each with a Python work: Adam Smith's invisible hand and Bentham's greatest-happiness utilitarianism fail in the 'Merchant Banker' sketch, where charity leaves the banker 'a pound down on the whole deal', while Marxist market ideology and alienation surface in the Communist Quiz and the accountant who longs to be a lion tamer. In The Holy Grail, Aristotle's doctrine of the mean sorts Brave Sir Robin's cowardly flight from Sir Lancelot's rash slaughter of a wedding party and Galahad's desire-distorted chastity at Castle Anthrax, with Bedevere's duck-weighing witch logic showing reasoning without judgment, and Arthur's quest collapses because 'strange women lying in ponds handing out swords is no basis for a system of government'. Life of Brian's 'blessed are the cheesemakers' and the 'You're all individuals!' crowd ground a Kantian demand for autonomy against blind obedience to religious rules. The Meaning of Life's 'Galaxy Song' and 'spiraling coils of self-replicating DNA' pose Nietzschean nihilism — science dissolving the highest values — which the film's closing advice to be nice to people and keep a sense of humor answers with a modest, livable meaning.

samples.title: H O N O R
samples.relation: This file gathers three Part One essays. Jacob Held reads Rorschach's 'evil must be punished' credo (drowning Big Figure, executing the multiple rapist) as Kantian retributivism: wrongdoers are punished because they deserve it, out of respect for their dignity and honor, punishment restoring the moral order (with Hegel) — and Rorschach's flaw is lacking the humility and checks that keep just deserts from degenerating into the Black Freighter's vengeance. Tony Spanakos applies Max Weber's definition of the state as the monopoly of legitimate violence to argue the Keene Act rightly criminalizes vigilantes like Rorschach and Veidt, and that even state-sanctioned heroes (the Comedian gunning down his pregnant Vietnamese lover, Dr. Manhattan's amoral ending of Vietnam) show a badge cannot make superhero coercion legitimate.
