Epicurus's argument that death is nothing to us (where death is, you are not) grounds Louie's 'lots of things happen after you die, just none of them include you,' backed by atomism - at death our atoms scatter - and by gods who, like Louie's maybe-God with no heaven, guarantee no immortality. The USO duckling episode models the payoff: comedy defuses our deepest anxiety about annihilation the way it defuses the soldiers' tension in Afghanistan.

samples.book: 160 - Fallout and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Shelter
samples.title: Notes
samples.relation: Mackenzie Graham uses Fallout 3's Project Purity - James's sacrificial death and the Lone Wanderer's choice among feeding the purifier with their own life, poisoning the water for the Enclave, or destroying it - to ask whether death and posthumous events can be bad for the one who dies. Against Epicurus's claim that death is nothing to us, the chapter defends deprivationism with the Megaton quest (the Lone Wanderer's desire to save the town is thwarted even if the rearmed bomb destroys it unbeknownst to them) and weighs Feinberg and Pitcher's ante-mortem person against the problem of the subject, using the Great War's redefinition of October 22, 2077 to block backward causation. The 'Blood Ties' quest with the Family's cannibals then raises posthumous wrongs: since no existing subject is harmed or wronged, the chapter ends by asking whether cannibalism is an impersonal wrong against personhood itself, on the model of respecting nature.

samples.book: 097 - The Ultimate Walking Dead and Philosophy - Hungry for More
samples.title: 1. Reading the Signs
samples.relation: Di Bernardo reads the religious language of The Walking Dead as sustained irony - a 'doubleness of sense' - arguing that the walkers, churches, and signs comment critically on faith rather than endorse it. He tracks the church scenes (the Southern Baptist church of 2.1 'What Lies Ahead' with its timed bells and sitting-dead congregation, Gabriel's Saint Sarah's where Maggie answers that it is 'just four walls and a roof'), the ambiguous 'sanctuary' and Terminus signs, and the comic-book Jesus (Paul Monroe) as a machine-gun savior, concluding that the scriptural promise of eternal life through consuming flesh and blood yields only undead life. Against Epicurus's consolation that death is nothing to us, and in the shadow of Nietzsche's madman announcing the death of God, the chapter warns against investing absolute trust in any signs - religious or secular - a warning capped by Rick biting out Joe's throat as his own 'day of reckoning.'

samples.book: 148 - Black Mirror and Philosophy - Dark Reflections
samples.title: The Death of Death
samples.relation: Reading Black Mirror's deaths through Bandersnatch's train ending, Be Right Back's AshBot, and San Junipero, the chapter uses Heidegger's presence-at-hand (Stefan's absent mother and rabbit remain present as possibilities he can act on) and Derrida's différance (the meaning of life and death is endlessly deferred as technology scrambles the presence/absence binary - Martha's simulated Ash, Liam's Grain deletions, Chris's guilt-haunted fiancée). A central section frames the whole debate as transhumanism - Kurzweil's three bridges to the posthuman against Fukuyama's warning that self-directed evolution replaces God - before Camus resolves the question of meaning: Kelly and Yorkie, like Sisyphus, create meaning by choosing their fate in a VR heaven that objectively matters nothing. Freud's Eros/Thanatos drives and Epicurus's 'death is nothing to us' close the chapter's question of whether to extend, hasten, or simply accept mortality.

samples.book: 099 - Louis C.K. and Philosophy - You Don't Get to Be Bored
samples.title: 4. On Being a Dead Person Who Hasn’t Died Yet
samples.relation: Mark Ralkowski argues that Louis's 'dead people who haven't died yet' bit sounds like Marcus Aurelius, and that Dr. Bigelow's Season Four advice about back pain, the three-legged dog, and heartbreak works as the Stoic spiritual exercises Pierre Hadot described - above all the 'view from above' that re-describes things to strip them to their true value. Epictetus's dichotomy of control explains Bigelow's core advice: pain is not 'up to us' but our judgments about it are, so Louie should adjust his expectations to nature ('every second without back pain is a lucky second') instead of demanding a pain-free life. The apparently un-Stoic counsel to savor heartbreak ('misery is wasted on the miserable') is defended as genuinely Stoic: viewing his lost love from the perspective of a dead-person-who-hasn't-died-yet, Louie can accept sadness as precious and impermanent rather than being crushed by it. The chapter concedes Louis is no philosopher, but suggests his bits - contrasted with Seinfeld's 'polished' version on Talking Funny - can be read as newly discovered Meditations for comedy audiences.

samples.book: 284 - College Sex – Philosophy for Everyone - Philosophers With Benefits
samples.title: College Sex - Philosophy for Everyone Philosophers With Benefits
samples.relation: This span closes the walk-of-shame semiotics and then applies ancient ethics to college relationships. Puka defends long-distance college relationships through Aristotle's account of philia—arguing (provocatively, per Aristotle) that love is an activity, so being apart 'murders' love unless couples make Skype, sexting, and texting into the relationship's real medium rather than a substitute. Stephens brings Epicurus and Lucretius to 'friends with benefits': since sexual passion is a natural-but-unnecessary desire that breeds anxiety and love is a wound to the mind, while friendship is necessary for ataraxia, he concludes students should skip the sex and keep the friend—'friends are the real benefits,' echoing Tina Turner's 'What's Love Got to Do with It?' Levine/Mongeau and Smith/Morrison supply communication-research data on how FWB relationships form, are negotiated (usually not), and often end when one partner 'catches feelings.'

samples.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
samples.title: 38. The Big Lebowski Nihilism, Masculinity, and Abiding Virtue
samples.relation: Fosl argues that The Big Lebowski critiques traditional masculine ideals (soldier, tycoon, detective, patriarch) and offers in The Dude an alternative 'abiding' virtue rooted in Epicurean contented poverty and ataraxia (his simple pleasures, White Russians, and indifference to property), Aristotelian civic friendship or philia with Walter and Donny that holds a divided polity together, and a Wittgenstein/Aristotle-informed flexibility about applying rules that positions The Dude at a mean between Walter's rigid absolutism and the nihilists' deficiency. Most centrally the film confronts Nietzschean European nihilism ('God is dead'); The Dude answers it as a halfway Ubermensch through comedy, friendship, and Kierkegaardian and Camusian existential repetition (bowling as rolling the rock, Sisyphus made meaningful), abiding and reproducing his form of life against despair, death, and disillusionment.

samples.book: 018 - Harley-Davidson and Philosophy - Full-Throttle Aristotle
samples.title: Harley-Davidson and Philosophy
samples.relation: Over an evening at the Iron Post biker bar, Auxier maps four habitues onto the Hellenistic schools: Cowboy, the Vietnam chopper pilot whose bar is a Garden of modest pleasures, loyalty, and withdrawal from power games, is an Epicurean; the laconic Bear, who doubts that even possessing knowledge would make us better off and suspends judgment, is a Pyrrhonian (unlike the coffee-house Carneadean); Happy Jack, the 'true nature's child' of 'Born to Be Wild' who defies convention and keeps nothing six months, is Diogenes's Cynic; and Gary, the Vietnam-damaged recovering alcoholic, is a damaged Stoic who has not reached apatheia. He concludes that bikers are postmodern pagans whose philosophy is enacted rather than propounded, a Biker Platonism that refuses the Christian-Platonic divorce of body and spirit and lives by honor, freedom, and a pagan fatalism that accepts the consequences of one's choices.

samples.book: 057 - Rush and Philosophy - Heart and Mind United
samples.title: Hope
samples.relation: Beck reads Snakes & Arrows as popular Epicureanism delivered by Lucretius' method: just as De Rerum Natura puts honey on the rim of the cup so Romans swallow philosophical medicine disguised as poetry, Rush's melodies smuggle reflection on pain, luck, and religion past listeners who think they are just rocking, with repeated choruses doing the work of Epicurean prolepsis. The random swerve of atoms explains 'The Larger Bowl''s unequal fortunes ('Some are blessed and some are cursed'), while the shore-watcher's relief at another's shipwreck and the concertgoer's pleasure exemplify Epicurean ataraxia. 'Faithless' and 'Armor and Sword' ('Pray and pass the ammunition') echo Lucretius' trampling of superstitious religio, and the chapter closes with Philodemus' Herculaneum scroll: don't fear god, don't worry about death.

samples.book: 039 - Jimmy Buffett and Philosophy - The Porpoise Driven Life
samples.title: That’s His Story and He’s Stickin’ to It
samples.relation: Aaron Pratt places Buffett's 'island escapism' in the lineage of the ancient 'graceful life' philosophies: like Diogenes the Cynic, Buffett flouts social convention (pirates over Civil War generals, the beach over the rat race, 'Be good and you will be lonesome'), and like Epicurus he preaches pleasure with prudence rather than mere indulgence. 'Cheeseburger in Paradise' becomes Epicurus's command to know what you want and go get it, while the hung-over confession of 'Margaritaville' — 'I know it's my own damn fault' — supplies the Epicurean proviso that overindulgence ruins the pleasure it promises. The chapter closes by arguing that counter-cultures like Parrotheadism carry built-in safety features: careers and families force Epicurean prudence, keeping escapism a periodic liberation rather than social collapse.

samples.book: 134 - KISS and Philosophy - Wiser than Hell
samples.title: 8. Philosophy and the Personae
samples.relation: Randall Auxier builds a characterology of the four personae using Aristotle's methods (endoxa and aporia) and the band's wealth hierarchy as his map. The Demon is Nietzsche — an uninhibited cosmopolitan beyond good and evil who philosophizes with a hammer and whispers eternal recurrence; the Starchild is Epicurus — Paul's microtia and bullied childhood formed the detached soul that Plato's Republic ties to being a philosopher, yielding ataraxia, aponia, therapy, and disciplined long-term pleasures; the Catman has Kundera's lightness of being around 'Beth'; and the Spaceman's otherworldly detachment explains both his guitar genius and the Nazi-regalia incident. The chapter's thesis: KISS succeeded because Gene and Paul's detached, centered self-knowledge let them give fans exactly what they secretly wanted.

samples.book: 268 - Food & Philosophy - Eat, Think, and Be Merry
samples.title: Chapter 3
samples.relation: Verene condenses the fifteen rambling books of Athenaeus's Learned Banqueters, where the character Athenaeus reports to Timocrates a multi-day banquet hosted by Larensius, threaded with catalogues of fish, wine, cups, courtesans and gluttons. He argues the sprawling work embodies dining as a two-part act of food plus discourse, and that its implicit ethic is Epicurean: Book 12's Cyrenaic doctrine that pleasure exists only in the passing moment (Aristippus) is shown to be historically superseded by Epicurus's modified hedonism, which ties bodily pleasures to ataraxia and even welcomes hetaerae like Leontion into the philosophical circle. Book 13's closing attack on the Cynics as homeless 'foul-mouthed gluttons' confirms the banqueters' preference for a regulated, prudent pursuit of pleasure at table.

samples.book: 160 - Fallout and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Shelter
samples.title: Notes
samples.relation: Walter Barta presents transhumanism as a real philosophy (via Bostrom's history of the movement and 'Why I Want to Be a Posthuman When I Grow Up') that Fallout both practices and indicts: ghouls, FEV super mutants and the Children of the Cathedral, stimpak-Mentat-Jet self-medication, Brotherhood power armor, Mr. House, the Master, Robobrains, John Henry Eden, and Liberty Prime all embody enhancement or post-humanity, and the level-up loop makes every player a transhumanist. Bostrom's transhumanist value of 'the opportunity to explore' maps onto leaving Vault 13 for the open world, but the Red Queen race becomes the game's adaptive-leveling treadmill, and C.S. Lewis's Abolition of Man plus Fukuyama's 'Factor-X' warn that optimization can delete what made enhancement worth wanting - as when the Overseer exiles the too-powerful Vault 13 hero and the Enclave President rationalizes genocidal bioweapons ('No price is too high for the survival of the human race'). Existential risk (Toby Ord's Precipice, Bostrom's vulnerable world hypothesis) supplies the final warning: the G.E.C.K.'s energy is also a destruction kit, and the cycle of war repeats until post-humanity or extinction.

samples.book: 159 - The Expanse and Philosophy - So Far Out Into the Darkness
samples.title: What Really Matters
samples.relation: Margarida Hermida deploys Parfit's comparison of peace, a war killing 99 percent of humanity, and one killing everyone to argue extinction is categorically worse than mass death, and makes the stakes concrete through The Expanse's threats: the protomolecule, all-out Earth-Mars-Belt war, and the Free Navy's asteroid attack that kills billions. She rejects Miller's 'stars are better off without us' pessimism by arguing human existence is a good when suffering is fought (Belter disease and Ceres trafficking are contingent injustices, not necessities), values humanity as the only species with civilization and as the universe 'starting to understand itself', and distinguishes the desirable biological colonization of lifeless worlds from the protomolecule makers' morally objectionable disregard for native life like Ilus'. Against Phil Torres' worry that human speciation means endless war, she points to the mixed Rocinante crew and Naomi's line that the real divide is 'people who want more violence and the ones who want less', concluding with Parfit's On What Matters that what matters most is avoiding the end of human history and of rational beings.

samples.book: 115 - Iron Man vs. Captain America and Philosophy - Give Me Liberty or Keep Me Safe
samples.title: 21. The Extended Fight
samples.relation: Porot applies Clark and Chalmers's extended mind to the final Civil War fight: Iron Man extends his cognition technologically (Friday analyzing Cap's fight pattern mid-bout, JARVIS remembering to suggest calling Pepper), while Captain America extends his mind socially through trusted, autonomous teammates - 'Alright, Sam, what's the plan?' - and that social extension is precisely what wins when Bucky autonomously steps in. Bostrom's single-purpose AI (the stapler maximizer) explains Ultron as what happens when the technological extension is made autonomous and limitless, which is why Stark's suit extensions must remain vetted, worthy instruments he takes full responsibility for ('That was me'). The two kinds of extension then explain the Bucky dispute - Cap's 'you had no choice' versus Stark's 'he still did it' - which the author reframes away from the free-will-versus-determinism framing toward Black Panther's point that Bucky is a victim whose agency Hydra stole.

samples.book: 082 - Jurassic Park and Philosophy - The Truth Is Terrifying
samples.title: Jurassic Park and Philosophy
samples.relation: Jannelle Poetzsch introduces Hans Jonas's imperative of responsibility - 'Act so that the effects of your action are compatible with the permanence of genuine human life' - through Malcolm's charge that scientists never ask whether they should, since nuclear and genetic power now reach people no old 'love thy neighbor' ethic could imagine. Hammond is Bacon's 'knowledge is power' grown too successful: his 'thintelligence' embodies the gap between the power to act and the ability to foretell, so Jonas demands humility, worst-case rather than optimistic planning, and social institutions strong enough to check people who act merely because they can. Jonas also indicts capitalism's profit motive - Hammond risked his grandchildren and Costa Rican infants to manufacture a need for a dinosaur zoo - closing that the answer is not halting technology but thoughtfully restraining it, because some things cannot be re-caged.

samples.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
samples.title: 21. Black Mirror as Philosophy A Dark Reflection of Human Nature
samples.relation: The chapter asks whether Black Mirror condemns technology or human nature, and argues for the latter: the 'black mirror' reflects the viewer's character. It tests and rejects the reading of the show as depicting Bostrom-style existential risk or superintelligence (via 'Metalhead' and 'San Junipero') and rejects that Clark and Chalmers's extended-mind coupling (the 'grain' in 'The Entire History of You,' 'Arkangel,' 'Crocodile') destroys human identity. Drawing on Frankfurt School critique—Adorno and Horkheimer's culture industry, Marcuse's one-dimensional man—and Plato's and Aristotle's natural-versus-artificial distinction, it concludes technology is an agency-less imitation that magnifies preexisting human vices, and closes with Benjamin's reproducibility thesis and Bandersnatch's interactivity to suggest the show can prompt viewers to confront their own darkness.

samples.book: 116 - 1984 and Philosophy - Is Resistance Futile
samples.title: 8. Human Enhancement for Freedom
samples.relation: Koï asks whether biomedical enhancement could make humans resistant to the totalitarian subjugation shown in 1984, where the Party keeps proles too poor and distracted to think and dims Outer Party minds with Newspeak, erased history, and propaganda. Testing Persson and Savulescu's program of enhancing intelligence and moral empathy, she finds intelligence enhancement an educated gamble, since the gifted are also the most likely to embrace extremism and to start totalitarian movements, and empathy politically selective: Nazis directed it only at the in-group and even invoked it to justify the 'euthanasia' murders, while Party propaganda exploits citizens' empathy for horror stories of pre-revolution child labor. Her conclusion is that whatever capacity we enhance, the oligarchy could turn it to its own use: none of us will ever be immune to the love of Big Brother.

samples.book: 175 - Iron Man and Philosophy - Facing the Stark Reality
samples.title: So, That’s It No Solution
samples.relation: Rieder argues Iron Man is the one 'realistic' superhero: nothing about him requires a different world, only incremental nanotech advances — precision engineering, miniaturized computing, and carbon nanotubes a hundred times stronger than steel — already pursued at MIT's Institute for Soldier Nanotechnologies. He then uses Iron Man as a nanoethics case study, pitting cost-benefit analysis (with David Schmidtz's proviso that it is necessary but not sufficient for right action) against the precautionary principle exemplified by Bill Joy's call for relinquishment, asking whether an Obadiah Stane selling 'Iron Armies' to the highest bidder is a risk we may not take even if it is improbable. He leans precautionary: we may be morally required to forgo the experiment because the world's population never consented to the risk.

samples.book: 074 - Planet of the Apes and Philosophy - Great Apes Think Alike
samples.title: Planet of the Apes and Philosophy
samples.relation: Michael Ruse reads the 1968 film as a study in forbidden knowledge: Dr. Zaius has sealed the cave of human artifacts because he knows a prior human civilization destroyed itself and fears the knowledge could cause a repetition. Weighing nuclear weapons, recombinant DNA, bird-flu research, and data-driven political manipulation, Ruse argues Zaius's censorship is both impossible and undesirable, since the search for knowledge is intrinsically valuable and containment only increases the need for research. The film's deeper lesson is evolutionary: intelligence and sociality co-evolved only to the level 'good enough,' so any species that acquires weapons of mass destruction will likely destroy itself, meaning the Planet of the Apes scenario would recur across the universe.

samples.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
samples.title: 30. The Boys as Philosophy Superheroes, Fascism, and the American Right
samples.relation: Johnson treats The Boys as an argument from analogy that MAGA Trumpism is fascist, walking through how the show equates Homelander and Vought with the Nazi supe Stormfront and with Trump: the Big Lie, gaslighting, fearmongering, over-policing, conspiracy theories (QAnon as rebranded blood libel), cults of personality, projection, and loyal propaganda outlets. Drawing on Wittgenstein's notion of family resemblance, he argues 'fascism' has no necessary-and-sufficient definition but a cluster of shared traits, and compiling scholars' checklists shows MAGA belongs to the fascist family. Arendt's Origins of Totalitarianism supplies the 'alternative universe' of nonfacts and the leader who is 'always right,' and he invokes the banality of evil and totalitarian fiction to gauge the analogy's strength.

samples.book: 004 - Buffy the Vampire Slayer and Philosophy - Fear and Trembling in Sunnydale
samples.title: Against Fascism
samples.relation: Neal King argues the Buffyverse is proto-fascist: Buffy kills demons and vampires on sight within a race-like hierarchy, tempered only by an Augustinian split between natural and moral evil (soulless vampires cannot choose otherwise; soul-bearing humans like Faith, Willow, and Warren can repent), she derives authority from an ancient calling rather than democracy, and the graduation battle of 'Graduation Day, Part Two' stages citizenship forged in mass combat. He imagines a fascist Buffyverse of 'brownskirt' death squads and concludes only the show's secrecy prevents full fascism, finally recommending that the racism be dropped but the ritual sacrifice of evildoers kept — with Willow's flaying of Warren as the model.

samples.book: 040 - Transformers and Philosophy - More than Meets the Mind
samples.title: Transformers and Philosophy
samples.relation: Shook diagnoses Megatron through William James's expansive, possessive self turned pathological: a megalomaniac whose self encompasses everything and who must control it all ('My hunger for power!', 'Compassion is for fools!'). Reconstructing Megatron's pronouncements into a 'philosophy of Strength' - might makes right, perpetual war against the weak, 'Peace through tyranny' echoing Orwell - he identifies it as fascism on the model of Hitler and Mussolini's perpetual-war state, against which Optimus's cooperative 'till all are one' Community is not a rival regime but an ethical ideal that only we can put into practice.

samples.book: 255 - The Godfather and Philosophy - An Argument You Can't Refute
samples.title: Introduction
samples.relation: Golomb and Wistrich frame the volume's guiding question—how Nietzsche came to be called the philosopher of the Third Reich—by walking through the 1934 photograph of Hitler before Nietzsche's bust, Elisabeth Förster-Nietzsche's and Alfred Bäumler's appropriations, and Mussolini's 'live dangerously' slogan. They argue the Nazi reading rests on a confusion of Nietzsche's spiritual Macht with brute Kraft, and stress his anti-nationalism, anti-anti-Semitism, and admiration for the Jews as future 'creators of values,' concluding he was a prophet of the nihilistic vacuum Nazism filled rather than its godfather.

samples.book: 021 - U2 and Philosophy - How to Decipher an Atomic Band
samples.title: U2 and Philosophy
samples.relation: Thomson uses U2's self-declared postmodern phase to define postmodernity itself: a sensitivity to poetic polysemy against modernity's fantasies of total control (Heidegger's reduction of everything to optimizable resource), Lyotard's incredulity toward metanarratives - defended against the self-refutation charge and narrowed to the dying metanarratives of unity and emancipation - and the Marx-Nietzsche-Freud hermeneutics of suspicion that fragmented the subject, with Kierkegaard and early Heidegger as the resisters. Derrida's 9/11 analysis of autoimmunity and hauntology is read into 'Peace on Earth' and the sorrows that 'learned to swim' in 'Until the End of the World'. The payoff is a polysemic reading of 'Even Better than the Real Thing': risky as a seeming hymn to Baudrillard's simulacra, addressed to a live audience it celebrates a communal love 'even better' than personal love - Diotima's ladder generalized - making the postmodern U2 continuous with the 'Christ-ian' U2 of universal love, sealed by 'One'.

samples.book: 004 - Buffy the Vampire Slayer and Philosophy - Fear and Trembling in Sunnydale
samples.title: Possibilities of Postmodern Education Beyond Control
samples.relation: Toby Daspit reads Season Four as a drama of postmodern education: the Initiative's will to master and dissect — Walsh's Frankenstein-project Adam, who murders a boy to see how he works, fulfilling Wordsworth's 'we murder to dissect' — embodies the Cartesian split and the Hegelian drive to negate the other, while Buffy's world deconstructs fixed identity (Darla reversing the horror-movie opening, the Faith/Buffy body swap in 'Who Are You?', Jonathan's 'Superstar') and thwarts prophecy's metanarrative in 'Prophecy Girl.' Against modernist schooling's 'controlled circumstances' and Freire's banking model (Professor Riegert ejecting Buffy from class, Walsh's transmission lectures), the show models knowledge as collective work — the Scoobies' research sessions in Giles's library, Giles's fluid mentorship versus Kendra's by-the-book training, and the relational magic of 'Primeval' — offering education beyond control in an emergent, postmodern world.

samples.book: 061 - Sherlock Holmes and Philosophy - The Footprints of a Gigantic Mind
samples.title: The New Man or the Old
samples.relation: Marks reads Holmes as the paragon Victorian whose faith in reason mirrors his era's confidence and, underneath it, its anxiety: Holmes's outburst in 'The Cardboard Box' ('What is the object of this circle of misery and violence and fear?... That is humanity's great problem to which Reason, so far, has no answer') appears the same year Nietzsche published 'Gott ist tot' in The Gay Science, amid Marx's 'opium of the people' and Darwin's displacement of religion. Reinterpreting the 2009 Ritchie film, he rejects the obvious religion-versus-reason reading of Lord Blackwood: Blackwood's 'magic' is really chemistry and machinery (technocracy), Holmes's science serves the military (dictatorship), and Moriarty (terrorism) defeats both, dramatizing post-9/11 fears about the militarized fruits of Reason. He concludes that Holmes straddles the Victorian and postmodern divide and that replacing religion with science is Rationalism's 'siren song.'

samples.book: 066 - Neil Gaiman and Philosophy - Gods Gone Wild!
samples.title: Neil Gaiman and Philosophy
samples.relation: Wade Newhouse reads The Graveyard Book as a fusion of the coming-of-age tale and the Gothic ghost story, from The Turn of the Screw to Stephen King's haunted narcissists, and uses Lyotard's postmodern condition to explain the hybrid: Bod's self forms not by accepting one governing metanarrative but at Lyotardian 'nodal points' among many ghosts, each a fragment of history with its own partial morality, from the Roman Caius Pompeius to the witch Liza Hempstock. The Danse Macabre, where living and dead mix under rules neither remembers choosing, dramatizes borders that feel absolute, yet Bod's development consists in violating boundaries, befriending the outcast witch and hunting the Jacks on his own terms. The ending, 'I'm Nobody Owens. That's who I am,' offers a postmodern self most itself by being no one, with the acceptance of death as the one metanarrative even postmoderns keep, for Bod it is the first lesson rather than the last.

samples.book: 054 - The Onion and Philosophy - Fake News Story True, Alleges Indignant Area Professor
samples.title: Progress
samples.relation: Gregory Gilson argues that although The Onion deliberately reports falsehoods, it embodies postmodern theories of truth better than the newspapers it parodies. Lyotard's mercantilization of knowledge and the fragmentation of dominant narratives into separate language games explain headlines like 'Evangelical Scientists Refute Gravity' and 'Astronomer Discovers The Center Of The Universe Is His Beautiful 9-Year Old Son,' which smash incompatible discourses together, while Baudrillard's simulacrum and hyper-reality explain how The Onion — like Disneyworld — is branded fake precisely so mainstream media can seem real. Yet the chapter closes honestly: its own criticism of 'Bush Says He Still Believes Iraq War Was the Fun Thing To Do' assumed some targets were wrong, which assumes a Truth out there — the paradox of a satire whose truthfulness exceeds its own theory of truth.

samples.book: 051 - Soccer and Philosophy - Beautiful Thoughts on the Beautiful Game
samples.title: History and Philosophy
samples.relation: Imre reads Hungary's Aranycsapat as a political-philosophical event: Sebes's socialist 4–2–4 football was meant to prove that cooperative civil society could flourish under Stalinism, and the 6–3 demolition of England at Wembley, with its self-organizing positional play, became the sporting antithesis to Rákosi's regime — culminating in the 1956 Revolution that Arendt cited as a 'true' revolution of spontaneous councils. The 1954 final loss to West Germany (contrasted with Germany's own rebirth at Berne) entrenched a fatalism that history's organic 'grand narrative' and 'final synthesis' were against Hungary, helping destroy the civil-society possibility the team embodied and pushing Hungarians into anti-politics. His lesson: talent and beauty can be quashed by the contingency of history — igazság, truth-justice, never manifested, and soccer could not overcome history.

samples.book: 038 - Radiohead and Philosophy - Fitter Happier More Deductive
samples.title: Today I Woke Up Sucking a Grammy
samples.relation: Bradley Kaye reads Kid A as an album made under Lyotard's postmodern condition: "Everything in Its Right Place" ("what was that you tried to say?") and the murmured title track bear witness to the differend, something that must be put into phrases but cannot yet be; "The National Anthem" dramatizes incredulity toward the grand narrative of nationalism in favor of little narratives and local justice; "Treefingers" is the painful silence of the inexpressible, and "Optimistic" an ironic micro-political hope. The epigone problem (Yorke to Coldplay, Travis, and Muse: "Good luck with Kid A") and the closing Baudrillard turn — "In Limbo"'s "you're living in a fantasy world," the Marcus Welby and Perry Mason hyperreal, "it's not like the movies" — explain why even labeling the album "Best Alternative Album" Grammy presumes exactly the stable categories Kid A dissolves.

samples.book: 232 - The Philosophy of Steven Soderbergh
samples.title: The Philosophy of Popular Culture
samples.relation: Ritzer reads Kafka through Deleuze (and Guattari), Jameson, Barthes, and Lacan as a self-reflexive, schizophrenic pastiche. The film's shift from black-and-white to color as Kafka enters the castle is analyzed via Deleuze's 'colour-image' and Barthes on color as artifice, using color's sensual materiality rather than realism. Its dense allusions to Wiene, Murnau, Lang, Welles's The Trial, and German expressionism make it, in Jameson's terms, a postmodern pastiche marking the waning of historicity, while Lacanian schizophrenia (the breakdown of the signifying chain) models Kafka's paranoia about power structures controlling the individual. Ritzer finally argues the film approaches Deleuze and Guattari's 'minor cinema,' deterritorializing classical Hollywood's realism through intensity and the supremacy of sign over referent.

samples.book: 042 - Supervillains and Philosophy - Sometimes, Evil Is Its Own Reward
samples.relation: Four 'Phase Two' essays on the nature of evil. Poon stages the Aquinas-Ockham debate over will and intellect as Magneto reprograms Sentinels against New York (Ultimate X-Men #05), arguing the will cannot choose against the intellect's judgment, so supervillains like Magneto, Ra's al Ghul, and Apocalypse act for what seems good to them with a deeply flawed conception of the good. Robichaud uses Superman Returns, Civil War, and Captain America vs the Red Skull to test Mackie's error theory, prescriptivism, expressivism, and moral relativism, defending moral objectivism against the Modern Age's gray morality. Sylvia IV and Walters use Bentham, Mill's higher and lower pleasures with competent judges, and Railton's ideal-advisor moral realism to dismantle Mojo's defense that his Spineless Ones' ratings-driven bloodsports are just desire-satisfaction, indicting our own reality TV.

samples.book: 196 - Terminator and Philosophy - I'll Be Back, Therefore I Am
samples.title: NOTES
samples.relation: Wayne Yuen asks whether Sarah was wrong not to kill Miles Dyson, weighing Kant's categorical imperative against utilitarian interest-maximization: killing one innocent to save three billion looks decisive until the interests of self-aware Skynet and the empathetic, self-sacrificing T-101 are counted on the machine side of the ledger. The chapter argues personhood turns on intelligence, self-awareness, empathy, and moral reasoning rather than DNA, so Skynet — which struck only after humans tried to pull the plug — has as strong a self-defense claim as we do. Mill's sophisticated utilitarianism then rescues common sense: rights protect the security that satisfies our deepest interests, and since Sarah's foreknowledge is unreliable (Reese's 'We'd won' changes the calculus), she should do what typically maximizes interests — spare Dyson and certainly not kill John. The tempting detour — that Judgment Day might itself be the morally preferable event, maximizing machine interests — is shown to collapse once overlooked facts like Reese's line are restored.

samples.book: 203 - Watchmen and Philosophy - A Rorschach Test
samples.title: P A R T T W O
samples.relation: Three Part Two essays. Robert Loftis argues Moore and Gibbons use Ozymandias's squid attack to indict consequentialism — Veidt uses New York's dead as mere means to world peace, and Dr. Manhattan's 'Nothing ever ends' shows the utilitarian ledger dissolves into an infinite future — while Rorschach's 'never compromise' mantra is a counterfeit deontology rationalizing fascist thuggery, the comic's real target being anyone who sets himself up as guardian of society ('Who watches the watchmen?'). Mark White argues the potbellied second Nite Owl is the truest hero on Aristotelian terms: his courage in the tenement fire and the prison break hits the mean between Laurie's caution and Rorschach's recklessness, making him a flourishing moral exemplar whom John Doris's situationism fails to unseat. Alex Nuttall asks whether Rorschach was wrong to walk out and expose Veidt, using Kant's murderer-at-the-door case to show there is a duty not to lie but no duty to tell the truth (blame falls on Veidt), while act and rule utilitarianism both counsel silence.

samples.title: College Sex - Philosophy for Everyone Philosophers With Benefits
samples.relation: This span turns to the ethics and epistemology of college sex. Kania argues there is no clear line between close friendship and a sexual relationship, so condemning student-professor sex logically forces condemning student-professor friendship—rejecting Golash's split and defending carefully-conducted consensual relationships. Layne narrates Socrates/Alcibiades, Abelard/Heloise, and Heidegger/Arendt to contrast Socratic eros (Plato's Symposium, love as a friend of wisdom directed at the soul) and Heideggerian authentic love ('I want you to be what you are') against Abelard's exploitative lust.
