Pinku weighs 'plain sex' against Nagel's interpersonal-arousal account of embodiment to ask whether sex needs love, and Brophy uses Kantian dignity (treating the body as a mere means, not an end) to argue that prostitution and webcam porn undertaken to pay tuition violate the student's autonomy.

samples.book: 122 - Westworld and Philosophy - Mind Equals Blown
samples.title: Whatever! It’s All Natural
samples.relation: Jaquet and Cova take the show's 'livestock' comparisons seriously and use animal ethics to test every justification for the guests' treatment of hosts. Direct speciesism (Logan: 'She's a goddamn doll') and indexical speciesism (Maeve's 'us versus them' to Bernard) both fail because mere species membership is morally irrelevant, like race or sex. The supposed human-exclusive markers also fail: hosts match us in intelligence (Maeve outclasses Stubbs), moral sense (Bernard's guilt over Theresa, Teddy's remorse over the massacre), and compatibilist free will - acts flowing from the agent's own desires - against Ford's determinism and Lutz's 'you don't have a choice.' They then refute the argument from nature (Ford's 'we murdered and butchered anything that challenged our primacy'), the Kantian person/tool contrast in the hosts' favor, Locke's creator-ownership ('I built your mind, Bernard'), and the 'better to exist' defense, concluding that because the hosts are conscious, they belong to the moral community alongside humans and animals.

samples.book: 031 - Johnny Cash and Philosophy - The Burning Ring of Truth
samples.title: Conclusion June Love Beyond the Jordan
samples.relation: Sennett builds "June Love" out of June Carter Cash's documented love, from the "Hurt" video's staircase glance to Rosanne Cash's eulogy that June saw your potential and "lifted them up" for you to see, and the love that steadied John through addictions and infidelity for thirty-five years. He stages the philosophy-of-love dilemma between appraisal theories (Velleman, grounding love in Kantian dignity that demands respect but cannot justify loving John rather than anyone) and bestowal theories (Irving Singer, on which love projects value and so cannot be justified at all), with Frankfurt's volitional account as a side note, and proposes June Love, loving the beloved's potentiality, as the hybrid that is both objective and active and can justify loving this person. He also distinguishes June Love from codependence: enabling entrenches the addict's destruction, whereas June's confronting-and-encouraging love, echoed in "Ring of Fire" and "Far Side Banks of Jordan," called Cash to transformation while leaving him himself.

samples.book: 104 - Red Rising and Philosophy - Break the Chains!
samples.title: 3. Hero or Villain
samples.relation: Kevin McCain asks whether Darrow the hero and Nero au Augustus the villain can really be told apart, noting both hold noble goals (Eo's dream versus preserving humanity) and share brutal means. Consequentialism fails to separate them: Darrow's sacrifice of dockworkers and Sons of Ares to Romulus mirrors Nero's 'I do what I need to do to protect the greater good,' and Harmony's sacrificing Evey shows the same ends-justify-means reasoning. Kantian ethics condemns both, since each lies to people and sacrifices them without consent, treating them as mere means to an end. Virtue ethics finally offers grounds: Aristotle's requirement of proper motivation, developed through Michael Slote, distinguishes Darrow, who acts from love for Eo, his friends, and the Colors and is wracked by guilt, from Nero, who is fueled by inhuman pride and feels nothing at Eo's hanging—so motivation may be what makes one forgivable and the other a villain, though the chapter ends wondering if good intentions pave the road to Hell.

samples.book: 164 - The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo and Philosophy - Everything Is Fire
samples.title: The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo and Philosophy
samples.relation: Salander shares Kant's detestation of the criminal's hypocrisy: Martin Vanger's meticulous, unimpulsive murders and Wennerström's hubristic paper trail fail the universal-law formulation because each supremely rational villain casts himself as the exception to rules that bind everyone else. But Salander fails Kant too—she hacks 'for the kick' rather than from duty, encroaches on innocent privacy, and takes justice into her own hands (tattooing Bjurman, stealing from and arranging the death of Wennerström) where Kant's 'On a Supposed Right to Lie' would forbid even lying to a murderer; the chapter finds her closest to Benjamin Constant's rejoinder that truth is owed only to those worthy of it, matching her maxim that 'a bastard is always a bastard.' Her strict promise-keeping, her cultivation of mind and body per the Doctrine of Virtue, and her refusal of guardianship and of Blomkvist's money make her, in Kantian terms, a champion of autonomy who is nonetheless a work in progress.

samples.book: 054 - The Onion and Philosophy - Fake News Story True, Alleges Indignant Area Professor
samples.title: Get Serious
samples.relation: David Kyle Johnson takes Nietzsche's suggestion that God is slowly dying and reads The Onion's religion stories — the faith healer who loses a patient during a routine miracle, Kansas fundamentalists lobbying to overturn the Second Law of Thermodynamics, and 'Evangelical Scientists Refute Gravity With New Intelligent Falling Theory' — as evidence of secularization. He splits blind faith (irrational belief despite evidence, as with Bush's 'Blind-Faith-Based Initiatives') from genuine faith as belief without sufficient evidence, arguing religion does science badly whenever it shields creationism from falsification. But science rests on unproven assumptions too, he shows via Hume's problem of induction, Descartes' skeptical problem, and Wittgenstein's charge that naming a 'strong nuclear force' explains no more than God pushing things down. Ockham's razor then decides for atheism — an unexplained universe is simpler than God plus a universe — though William James's will to believe leaves a door open for faith where evidence is impossible, qualified by Clifford's warning that beliefs likely to harm others are never permissible.

samples.book: 046 - Mr. Monk and Philosophy - The Curious Case of the Defective Detective
samples.title: Is Monk’s Certainty Justified
samples.relation: Rauhut tests Monk's method against two models of discovery: Holmes-style eliminatism, modeled on Popper's falsification via reductio ad absurdum, and CSI-style confirmationism in the mold of Hempel and Carnap (Gil Grissom letting evidence speak). Monk fits neither — in 'Mr. Monk and the Astronaut' he refuses to eliminate the alibi-solid Steve Wagner, and in 'Mr. Monk Falls in Love' he ignores a hatpin, a motive, and a confession pointing at Leyla. Instead Monk is an 'epiphanist': he registers every anomaly (the secretary hired from a Lamaze-class ad in 'Mr. Monk Fights City Hall', Crawford's odd phrasing 'No, she wouldn't be drinking now'), suddenly sees the one theory explaining all of them, and only afterwards manufactures shareable evidence for others. His absolute certainty, the chapter argues, rests on a metaphysical faith that only the true theory can explain every anomaly — a Leibnizian 'best of all possible ordered worlds' — the same obsession with order that makes him notice anomalies at all, though it makes him epistemically irresponsible by ordinary standards that weigh alternative hypotheses and simplicity.

samples.book: 201 - Veronica Mars and Philosophy - Investigating the Mysteries of Life (Which Is a Bitch Until You Die)
samples.title: When Life Gives You Chlamydia
samples.relation: Andrew Zimmerman Jones explains Veronica's casework as inductive reasoning: Occam's razor dispatches Meryl's 'space laser' speculation and identifies Gia's stalker via the simplest explanation (the stalker drove off in the pick-up), while Keith's refusal to accept Abel Koontz's confession shows the razor's limits — Sheriff Lamb's laziness being Sidney Brenner's 'Occam's broom,' whisking inconvenient facts like Lilly's body temperature under the rug. Distinguishing Aristotle's particulars-to-universal induction from deduction, the chapter teaches the probability fallacy through the Mercer evidence (clippers, cologne, and GHB make it likely the rapist owns them, not that their owner is the rapist — the same confusion fueling suspicion of PCH-ers) and catalogues the fallacies — false dilemma, false cause, ad hominem, appeal to emotion — that Veronica's jealousy-driven reasoning commits in the Sully case. The chlamydia diagnosis revealing Cassidy raped her is the final lesson: new evidence overturns even well-confirmed conclusions, so certainty is a sucker's bet.

samples.book: 178 - LEGO and Philosophy - Constructing Reality Brick by Brick
samples.title: Notes
samples.relation: Leuenberger argues that a LEGO MOC is a surprisingly faithful model of David Lewis's Humean supervenience: the world is just a vast mosaic of local matters of particular fact — homogeneous, arbitrarily recombinable atomic bricks (fundamental properties at space-time points) with no necessary connections, Hume's 'greater denier', versus gunky Play-Doh or jigsaw pieces. Ockham's Razor motivates the view (while also able to cut against a divine master builder, whom Lewis's world lacks, though LEGO-world builders likewise stand outside their creations), and Lewis's concrete possible worlds make every build a replica rather than a creation, answered to the 'incredulous stare' by quantitative parsimony. Four-dimensionally stacked creations model change as variation along temporal parts, while the causation objection — nothing in one LEGO creation brings about the next — marks the fundamental Humean/non-Humean divide.

samples.book: 075 - Psych and Philosophy - Some Dark Juju-Magumbo
samples.title: Psych and Philosophy
samples.relation: Guidry-Grimes treats Chief Vick's hiring of Shawn as a genuine problem in applied ethics rather than a joke: the Psi hypothesis fails Ockham's Razor and no controlled study supports paranormal ability, yet Vick - unlike viewers who know Shawn is a fraud - must weigh her obligations to victims, the department, and taxpayers on the evidence she has. The chapter argues that hiring Shawn is ethically defensible given his record of solving over fifty unsolvable cases, but it catalogues the costs: false hope for distraught families (Marc Klaas's resentment of psychic tipsters), damage to Lassiter's morale, wasted resources, and the fragile public trust bound up with taxpayer money. The conclusion is a compromise: Vick is ethically required to use every tool in the arsenal, including a successful 'psychic,' only in desperate high-stakes cases where the victim's family does not object, and otherwise merely permitted.

samples.book: 196 - Terminator and Philosophy - I'll Be Back, Therefore I Am
samples.title: NOTES
samples.relation: Richard Brown uses the title 'The Terminator' itself to run the debate over definite descriptions: Russell's theory of descriptions makes 'The Terminator can't be bargained with' false (there are many T-101s, and no real-life Terminator at all), while Strawson insists Kyle's utterance genuinely refers to the machine at the door. Donnellan's referential/attributive distinction is staged through Lieutenant Traxler's 'The phone book killer has no pity' — true of whoever fits the description, or of the very Terminator Sarah has in mind — and Kripke's arguments from 'Russell English,' anaphora, and indirect quotation are weighed against Devitt's pronoun-of-laziness and reference-borrowing replies. The chapter sides with Grice's modified Ockham's razor: descriptions are not semantically ambiguous, so the title is literally false but apt, since Cameron referentially means the T-101.

samples.book: 118 - Scott Adams and Philosophy - A Hole in the Fabric of Reality
samples.title: 7. Scott Adams’s Joy of Logic
samples.relation: Bilsker turns Adams's Joy of Work catalogue of irrational co-workers into a critical-thinking syllabus: faulty analogy (from dogs fetching sticks to potatoes dancing, and Francis Bacon's body-politic passage praising war as exercise), huge-pants faulty causation, the Reinhart-Rogoff debt paper that drove austerity policy on mere correlation until Herndon, Ash, and Pollin exposed it, complex and objectionable cause, the overapplication of Occam's Razor to moon-landing hoaxes, misplaced authority, begging the question, and egocentric biases like I Am the World. He then contrasts the classroom view that confirmation bias is an unconscious background program with Win Bigly's claim that bias is the operating system itself, worrying about the implication that reasoning with anyone is futile, and concludes that Adams overstates how incapable we are of overcoming our biases.

samples.book: 074 - Planet of the Apes and Philosophy - Great Apes Think Alike
samples.title: Planet of the Apes and Philosophy
samples.relation: Don Fallis proposes deception rather than language as the personhood test: following Dennett, a deceiver must be a second-order intentional system who can want someone else to have a false belief, as when General Thade lies to Senator Sandar about Ari's kidnapping, Zira and Cornelius feign muteness before the Presidential Commission, and Caesar fakes his own electrocution in Conquest. The roles' reversal makes this a test for the films' mute humans too, while Descartes's beast machines, Wittgenstein on dogs that cannot simulate pain, and Lloyd Morgan's canon voice the skeptical reading of fake alarm calls and Koko's 'Cat did it.' Against them Fallis invokes Occam's Razor over Hare, Call and Tomasello's food-competition experiments: apes track who sees what, but they fail the misinformed false-belief version, so real apes may not be 'sneaky enough to be people.'

samples.book: 189 - The Ultimate Star Trek and Philosophy - The Search for Socrates
samples.title: Notes
samples.relation: Charts Star Trek's handling of secularization, from the "Roddenberry attitude" of Kirk confronting fifteen would-be gods to later series' complications, using Robert Audi's nine features of religion and Benedict Anderson's "imagined community" - the Yangs' sacred flag and worship-word "freedom" in "The Omega Glory" show an incoherent civic religion Kirk can correct. "Who Watches the Watchers" inverts the dynamic by making Picard an accidental god who refuses to found a religion among the proto-Vulcan Mintakans, while real-world creationism in schools and abstinence-only sex education supply the chapter's empirical moral arguments that faith-driven public policy fails on its own terms. DS9's Bajor arc - Vedek Winn boycotting Keiko's school, Sisko's defense of the faith that sustained Bajor through occupation, and Akorem's restoration of the D'jarra castes in "Accession", likened to Plato's Republic-class soul hierarchy - grounds the claim that infallible religious authority corrodes democratic equality, with Sisko as the Emissary who synthesizes faith and secular governance.

samples.book: 051 - Soccer and Philosophy - Beautiful Thoughts on the Beautiful Game
samples.title: How Beckenbauer and Zidane Practiced the Four Cardinal Virtues
samples.relation: Coumoundouros explains soccer greatness through three Platonic ideas: the Form of the footballer, which Pelé (1,281 goals, three World Cups, the save by Banks his header 'infected' with greatness and the infamous miss against Uruguay) and Maradona (the Hand of God and the Goal of the Century past five English defenders) approximate as near-perfect imitations, with position-specific Forms like forward Form for Pelé and attacking-midfielder Form for Maradona. Excellence as performing a proper function well (Republic 353a) then accounts for modern players—Ronaldo's evolved winger role, Henry converted by Wenger into a striker, Marta averaging a goal per game proving women's soccer equals the men's. Finally the Republic's four cardinal virtues grounded in the tripartite soul apply off and on the pitch: Beckenbauer playing the 1970 'Game of the Century' with a fractured clavicle and marshaling the 1974 final shows courage, wisdom, and moderation in just balance, while Zidane's 2006 head-butt on Materazzi shows the spirited part overwhelming reason, and with it greatness itself.

samples.book: 163 - Game of Thrones and Philosophy - Logic Cuts Deeper Than Swords
samples.title: Game of Thrones and Philosophy
samples.relation: Eric Silverman argues Game of Thrones explodes the storybook link between virtue and worldly happiness: Ned, 'one man in ten thousand,' is betrayed and executed, so Plato's claim that the just person is happy must mean psychic order rather than material flourishing - reason ruling spirit and appetite - as with Bran, who flourishes as a greenseer though he will never walk again. Cersei is Plato's tyrant, her soul ruled by insatiable appetite and paranoia, so no external goods can ever satisfy her, while Aristotle's correction - virtue necessary but not sufficient for eudaimonia, which also needs health, friends, and good fortune - explains why both Ned (virtue without external goods) and Cersei (goods without virtue) end up unhappy. Finally he inverts Pascal's Wager: since playing the game of thrones risks total loss (torture, humiliation, death) for limited gain, and even winning hollows you out - Robert confesses he was 'never so alive as when I was winning this throne or so dead as now that I've won it' - only a fool would play.

samples.book: 182 - Mad Men and Philosophy - Nothing Is as It Seems
samples.title: “I’m Enjoying the Story So Far, but I Have a Feeling It’s Not Going to End Well”
samples.relation: South uses 'New Amsterdam' to examine how social convention, not personal authority, constrains agency: Bert Cooper's 'New York City is a marvelous machine' and 'There are other rules... His mother is Dorothy Dyckman Campbell' reveal that Pete's value lies in a name he doesn't understand, just as Don's authority dissolves before forces neither he nor Pete consented to. Reading through Plato's Republic city-soul analogy and Adeimantus's warning that changes in music insinuate themselves 'little by little' into character and laws, the chapter shows Pete missing the worth of his old-family name, the Bethlehem Steel man missing that steel cannot be advertised like flour, and Don, despite seizing a fresh identity, quietly conforming to the suburban corporate script he claims never to have envisioned. The Kennedy-assassination pitch to Peggy ('The way that they saw themselves is gone') and Conrad Hilton's 'It's business' close on Plato's caution: the city's gears keep turning, and 'people don't change' may be the show's last word.

samples.book: 170 - House and Philosophy - Everybody Lies
samples.title: Notes
samples.relation: Argues House of Cards is a modern version of the Sophistical challenge in Books 1-2 of Plato's Republic: Thrasymachus' claim that justice is the advantage of the stronger and the unjust life is preferable. It maps Frank's proprietary 'my people' attitude and his shepherd-and-flock use of Russo, Stamper, Sharp, Meechum and his Gaffney constituents onto Thrasymachus' reversal of Socrates' shepherd analogy, and reads the Secretary of State snub, Blythe's naivety and Dunbar's descent into dirty tricks as proofs that the just are dupes. Frank's Sentinel ring and 'craft' make him Glaucon's perfectly unjust man of the Ring of Gyges story — unjust while seeming just — while the framed Lucas Goodwin plays the perfectly just man punished for a reputation for injustice. The chapter ends by arguing Frank falls short of the ideal tyrant (his conscience, his church visits asking 'what Justice is') and is coming to live the Book 9 tyrant's friendless 'worst sort of life' as Claire and the others abandon him.

samples.book: 074 - Planet of the Apes and Philosophy - Great Apes Think Alike
samples.title: Planet of the Apes and Philosophy
samples.relation: Greg Littmann maps Ape City onto Plato's Republic class by class: orangutan rulers who legislate, censor, and propagandize; gorilla warriors who enforce; chimpanzee producers who do all the work - including, pointedly, the science Plato made no provision for; and humans as the 'barbarians' Plato says may be enslaved or exterminated. The overlaps are detailed: the Sacred Scrolls' first article of faith functions as the noble lie's myth of the metals, orangutan funerals promise heaven to keep gorillas unafraid of death, and Zaius's erasing of Taylor's dust-writing and blowing up of the archaeological cave enact the rulers' duty to supervise stories. But the films also refute Plato: hereditary orangutans show that power corrupts philosopher kings, Dr. Honorius's 'reason' is dogma serving the faith, the gelding threat that finally breaks Taylor cracks the tripartite-soul analogy of justice, and democracy's rough virtue is that it lets us remove rulers 'without sticking anybody with iron spears.'

samples.book: 094 - Divergent and Philosophy - The Factions of Life
samples.title: 8. Plato’s Chicago
samples.relation: Littmann systematically maps Roth's Chicago onto Plato's Republic: like Marcus, Plato rejects democracy after Athens executed Socrates; both dissolve the family ('faction before blood' versus children raised in common and bred by state schedule); Erudite's IQ-selected leadership mirrors the rigorously trained philosopher-rulers, Dauntless the warrior class whose purely physical training Plato warns turns 'savage and harsh,' Abnegation's poverty the guardians's communism of property, and the factionless the powerless producers - with Plato's noble lie about the metals matching the Erudite's propaganda and serums as instruments of control. The shared flaw, he argues, is concentrated power without external checks, which corrupted Abnegation, corrupts every Dauntless leadership change, and would corrupt Plato's guardians too. The lesson is not to hand power to the least vicious but for democratic voters to confront their own ignorance - or end like Roth's America, in apocalyptic war.

samples.book: 037 - The Wizard of Oz and Philosophy - Wicked Wisdom of the West
samples.title: Dorothy and the Art of War
samples.relation: The Bells read Baum's book against Bleeding Kansas and John Brown: 1900 readers, they argue, heard 'Kansas' as the slave-or-free question, making Dorothy the Great Emancipator who frees the Munchkins, the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, the Winkies, and finally herself from the Witch's servitude. They pair her with Socrates, recasting the Republic's opening scene at Cephalus's slave-owning mansion (Thrasymachus's 'injustice on a sufficiently large scale' pays) as an abolitionist confrontation, and quoting the Phaedo's claim that philosophy is practicing for death to explain why vastly outnumbered reformers—Socrates, Brown at Harpers Ferry and Osawatomie, Dorothy facing the Witch's forty wolves, forty crows, bee swarms, and Winkie army—do not fear the odds. The shared moral: the love of wisdom, pursued in a community of inquirers, charms away the fear of death, which is why tyrants and slave-owners, whose own best part is enslaved, live in terror and cannot sleep at night.

samples.book: 037 - The Wizard of Oz and Philosophy - Wicked Wisdom of the West
samples.title: Roll Credits
samples.relation: Dunn contrasts Baum's book, where evil is wonderfully 'small'—Dorothy melts the Witch in a fit of righteous anger at a stolen Silver Shoe, and personal plus social virtues (kindness repaid by the field-mice Queen) reliably conquer it—with the 1939 film, which smuggles back the 'heartaches and nightmares' Baum banished and resolves the Witch only by an accidental stroke of luck. He sorts Oz's harms into moral evils (the Witch's enslavements, the Wizard's frauds) and natural evils (the cyclone, the Deadly Poppy Field), cites Hume's catalogue of the world's ills, and observes that Baum needs neither Kant's postulate of God and a future life to join virtue with happiness nor John Hick's 'vale of soul-making' theodicy—Oz simply delivers the reward. Dorothy's abundant virtue at age five rebukes Aristotle (children, he says, cannot be virtuous or happy) and instead embodies Rousseau's Emile, natural goodness uncorrupted by civilization, while Chesterton's Doctrine of Conditional Joy and Tolkien's insistence on serious, non-technological magic frame the Old-World Christian outlook that Baum's demystified American fairy tale—and the movie's ending—quietly betray.

samples.book: 043 - The Golden Compass and Philosophy - God Bites the Dust
samples.title: The Golden Compass and Philosophy
samples.relation: Robison measures Pullman's Authority against the three attributes that make the Christian God worthy of worship and finds it fails all three: the suffering of intercision victims like Tony Makarios and the Authority's delegation to the malevolent Metatron defeat omnibenevolence, because unlike with the real God we know no free-will theodicy applies, since the Authority simply does not care; his ignorance of Lyra's destiny (which witches and the Consistorial Court learn long before he does) defeats omniscience; and his demented weeping in the crystal litter before dissolving in open air defeats omnipotence. Since the Authority never created the universe and lied about being its creator, he is not God at all, so Pullman's plot never refutes the God of the philosophers. What the books do establish, she argues, is a powerful attack on organized religion: the Magisterium's suppression of Dust research and harming of children mirror real religious institutions' punishment of Galileo, resistance to evolution, and persecution of dissenters.

samples.book: 021 - U2 and Philosophy - How to Decipher an Atomic Band
samples.title: U2 and Philosophy
samples.relation: Wrathall's introduction argues U2 is philosophically interesting because its enormous popularity holds up a mirror to what 'we' care about (by Nietzsche's test of how a culture stands toward life) and because the band publicly wrestles with the contradictions of the technological-global economy: unprecedented freedom of choice paired with loss of rooted identity, and distant suffering ('Crumbs from Your Table') that we feel both powerless to fix and responsible for. Its showcase reading treats 'Miracle Drug' as a musical theodicy: Bono's plea 'God, I need your help tonight' is answered by the Edge's guitar and by the Matthew 25:35 refrain, so science and medicine count as works of Christian charity. The piece then frames the volume's essays: Plato's ascent of love in the early songs, Kierkegaardian despair after Achtung Baby, Bono's search for authentic identity, the simulacra of 'Even Better than the Real Thing', being-toward-death in the apocalyptic songs, and the Plato-versus-Aristotle quarrel over music's emotional power.

samples.book: 079 - Frankenstein and Philosophy - The Shocking Truth
samples.title: Frankenstein and Philosophy
samples.relation: Trip McCrossin casts the creature as a modern Job: repeatedly and unreasonably mistreated by the De Laceys, the rustic whose child he saved, and Victor despite his benevolence, he cries 'This was then the reward of my benevolence!' - but unlike Job he loses faith, because his problem of evil is secular, justifying not 'the Ways of God to Man' but 'the Ways of Man to monsters.' The chapter traces the problem from Job and Paradise Lost through Bayle's defense of faith over reason and the Optimists' 'best of all possible worlds,' whose credibility drowned with the 1755 Lisbon earthquake, setting Rousseau against Voltaire: Rousseau's Emile ('All is good leaving the hands of the author of things') demands that we make evil intelligible through self-knowledge, while Candide counsels tending our garden. The creature embodies Rousseau's line - 'I was benevolent and good; misery made me a fiend' - yet ends in self-abhorring remorse over Victor's death, leaving open whether self-knowledge can ever answer unreasonable suffering.

samples.book: 096 - Hannibal Lecter and Philosophy - The Heart of the Matter
samples.title: 4. Acts of God
samples.relation: McCrossin reads Lecter's parable of the church collapses - 'It must feel good to God - He does it all the time, and are we not made in His image?' - as Lecter's solution to the problem of evil in both its theological (Job) and secular (Neiman) forms: a malevolent deity of the kind de Sade's Saint-Fond describes, doing God's work becomes Lecter's justification, and killing feels good because 'if one does what God does enough times, one will become as God is'. Following Neiman, he sets Rousseau's tradition (evil must be made intelligible - 'All is well leaving the hands of the author of things') against Voltaire's Candide refusal of theodicy, showing that Will and Starling live in Rousseau's camp except when facing Lecter himself, and that the Hannibal/Hannibal Rising revelation that Mischa's murder 'happened' to him radically revises his earlier claim that 'we don't invent our natures', with Starling's reason finally making 'a place for Mischa' in Lecter and Starling together.

samples.book: 038 - Radiohead and Philosophy - Fitter Happier More Deductive
samples.title: Thinking in Rainbows
samples.relation: Jason Lee reads Hail to the Thief as a metaphysics of evil anchored in blurred boundaries between self and other: the "radiohead" conceit (Descartes' inert matter vs. thinking souls, Bowie's Thomas Newton) makes the sentient android of "Paranoid Android" the emblem of a self porous to signals and control, while "Where I End and You Begin" ("I will eat you alive") locates evil in the feared Other, glossed through Heidegger's das Nichts (evil as lack, not a thing) and Foucault's account of Enlightenment reason classing unreason as inhuman. He hears "Sit Down. Stand Up." as Auschwitz ("the raindrops could be gas") and "Go to Sleep" via The Wicker Man's human sacrifice, then argues The Most Gigantic Lying Mouth of All Time and Yorke's turn to Friends of the Earth and pay-what-you-want In Rainbows show philosophy is no longer sovereign: discourse with the Other is "responsibility, the call to respond ethically" — you have not been paying attention, so act before it's too late.

samples.book: 131 - Avengers Infinity Saga and Philosophy - Go for the Head
samples.title: 8. Time Travel and the Problem of Evil
samples.relation: Ray Bossert reads Endgame through Boethius's Consolation of Philosophy, arguing that Doctor Strange and Tony Stark, who permit the Snap and five years of suffering for the sake of the one winning outcome, run 'uncannily parallel' to Thanos, who decided for Gamora that her unwilling death served the greater good. Strange's viewing of 14,000,605 futures illustrates Boethius's distinction between an infinite being riding along the timeline and an eternal one seeing all moments at once, and the refusal to tell Stark his role mirrors why God's foreknowledge sees our choices without compelling them. Boethius's providence weaving free choices into justice, the Avengers' passion-driven failures on Titan (Star-Lord and Thor avenging lost lovers), justice as the wicked's own punishment (Thanos dying wretched twice in one film), and Umberto Eco's 'Myth of Superman' all frame a universe where suffering is allowed because it is woven into a pattern that ends in justice.

samples.book: 188 - The Ultimate South Park and Philosophy - Respect My Philosophah!
samples.title: THE ULTIMATE SOUTH PARK AND PHILOSOPHY
samples.relation: Johnson formalizes Kyle's crisis in 'Cartmanland'—evil Cartman inherits a million dollars and buys the amusement park while good Kyle suffers hemorrhoids and loses faith—as a valid argument from the logical problem of evil, then evaluates the town's theodicies against the philosophical ones. The Job story Kyle's parents read him fails like skeptical theism (it proves too much and ends in moral agnosticism), Chef's 'sweet milk of our tears' mirrors Calvin's and Edwards's God-glorifying account, Stan's restored faith via Cartman's perfect misery is a greater-goods response, Augustine's free will defense purchases goodness at the price of God's control of prayers and elections and cannot explain natural evils, and Hick's soul-making theodicy founders on fawns, tsunamis, and Kenny's deaths. Pascal's Wager and Plantinga's divine sense are dismissed in turn: evil does not disprove God, but proportioning belief to evidence makes non-belief the rational stance.

samples.book: 019 - Monty Python and Philosophy - Nudge Nudge, Think Think!
samples.title: A Nietzschean Conclusion
samples.relation: Slowik argues the Pythons have a positive existentialist message: Kafka's bureaucratic insanity, where ordinary people beat helplessly against irrational rules, recurs in the 'Cheese Shop' and 'Dead Parrot' sketches, and Camus's Sisyphus lives on in the monotonous lives of Palin's city stockbroker and the accountant who dreams of lion taming — repetition without Sisyphus's defiance. The core claim is that Python endorses individual-centered existentialism: Brian's 'You've got to think for yourselves. You're all individuals!' is the troupe's rare direct statement of Sartre's 'existence precedes essence', confirmed by Cleese's and Palin's interviews about resisting those who tell you how to behave, a theme the chapter extends through Nietzsche's critique of moral tradition and organized Christianity. Sartrean bad faith explains Python's stereotyped characters — the aggressive policeman, the pepperpots, and Mr. Praline insisting 'I am not a loony!' while demanding a fish license for his halibut — while Arthur Pewtey's meek 'Right. Right.' and Ron Obvious's physical limits raise nature/nurture objections to Sartrean freedom. The 'Nietzschean Conclusion' is that Monty Python itself exemplifies will to power as 'giving style' to one's character, constantly overcoming its own formulas rather than repeating what succeeded.

samples.book: 129 - RuPaul's Drag Race and Philosophy - Sissy That Thought
samples.title: 16. Death Becomes Her
samples.relation: Hendrik Kempt reads Drag Race's pervasive death imagery - death-drops, the 'lip sync for your life,' mirror messages, the 'Death Becomes Her' runway - through the philosophy of death. Epicurus's 'death is nothing to us' and Stoic self-possession (Ru's 'pay them bitches no mind,' Violet Chachki enduring a tiny corset) explain why elimination, like death, gives no ground for worry once it arrives, while Socrates' 'philosophy is training for death' makes the show a workout video for dying - Socrates even dying fussing over a rooster like a drag mother to Miss Fame. Heidegger's thrownness and being-toward-death set up Sartre's radically free, future-oriented self - so voluntary exits like BenDeLaCreme's self-elimination and Charlie Hides's listless lip-sync betray one's own plans - and Camus's Sisyphus makes Chi Chi DeVayne and Roxxxy Andrews's doomed All Stars returns models of 'acceptance without resignation.' The closing weighs transhumanism's promise of conquered death against a DragCon-forever thought experiment, concluding with Ru's roast eulogy for Lady Bunny that love and irreverence, not immortal life, are the point.

samples.book: 038 - Radiohead and Philosophy - Fitter Happier More Deductive
samples.title: How to Misunderstand Politics Completely
samples.relation: Melançon argues Radiohead's real politics lie not in the overt content of Hail to the Thief but in a Camusian movement from absurdity to revolt: 'Exit Music'''s violent shift from Romeo's tender 'you' to the distorted 'we hope that you choke' enacts revolt against imposed rules and wisdom, while the android of 'Fitter Happier' ('a pig in a cage on antibiotics') and the wished-for alien of 'Subterranean Homesick Alien' dramatize absurd life under others' dictates. Following The Myth of Sisyphus and The Rebel — 'I revolt, therefore we are' — he shows how the songs' 'I' becomes a collective 'we' ('Karma Police', 'Lucky', 'Dollars and Cents') whose revolt, like Sisyphus's conscious walk back down the mountain, affirms life without ever justifying murder. Merleau-Ponty's philosophy of expression then explains why the songs are political anyway: artists express a still-unspoken 'fever' (it took years before 'Nude' could be said), creating a public and a common world — politics as unveiling rather than governing, down to 'Electioneering'''s admission that the band too campaigns for our vote.

samples.book: 046 - Mr. Monk and Philosophy - The Curious Case of the Defective Detective
samples.title: Mr. Monk Meets Alexander the Great
samples.relation: Wittkower argues that Monk's daily, unwinnable war on dirt and disorder is Camus's happy Sisyphus made concrete: Monk vacuums ceilings, touches lampposts, and solves murders knowing the dirt and the murderers will always return ('There's never hope... Hope. I hate hope's guts' in 'Mr. Monk Can't See a Thing'), yet he still finds enough satisfaction to take up the wipe again. Reading Ecclesiastes' vanity alongside the uncaring wasp of the opening, the chapter claims Monk shows us how to live wisely without resignation in an absurd world that does not care. He is paired with Diogenes the Cynic, whose barrel, raw onions, and midday lantern mirror Monk's pot-pie-Tuesdays and his refusal to overlook what everyone else ignores; like Diogenes telling Alexander the Great 'get out of my sun,' Monk lives by his own ideals no matter how society judges him. The essay closes that, like Camus addressing the Dominican monks, we should refuse to 'be reasonable' about evil and disorder and keep struggling without hope, wipe in hand.

samples.book: 030 - Pink Floyd and Philosophy - Careful with that Axiom, Eugene!
samples.title: Would You Help Me to Carry the Stone
samples.relation: Weinstein argues critics who call Waters a gloomy misanthrope misread him: he is an existentialist whose work maps point for point onto Camus's absurd, the human demand for unity endlessly frustrated. Waters's imagery tracks Camus's: the sun (Plato's cave symbol of the good, and the light Sisyphus loved on earth) against the eclipsed moon of death and madness; the stone we secrete through failed communication ('the bad blood slows and turns to stone' in 'Dogs,' 'would you help me to carry the stone' in The Wall) against Sisyphus's rock; and Pink's Trial, condemned for 'showing feelings of an almost human nature,' replaying Meursault's condemnation for failing to cry at his mother's funeral. Since the institutions of home, school, military, and the music industry's machine block every genuine encounter, Waters's persistence in making art that mostly fails to communicate is itself the absurd revolt, so with Camus one must imagine Sisyphus happy, and Weinstein imagines Waters happy too.

samples.book: 202 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Shotgun. Machete. Reason
samples.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
samples.relation: Rachel Robison-Greene applies Camus's absurdity to the series: walkers, like digger wasps, live meaningless loops without the self-reflective consciousness that 'poisons' experience, while survivors like Morgan longing for Jenny and Andrea for fishing trips with her father embody the clash between human longing and an indifferent universe, exactly as in Camus's The Plague at Oran. Suicide (Jacqui and Jenner as the CDC explodes) and religious consolation are escapist responses—the latter 'philosophical suicide'—so the authentic path is the absurd hero: Rick searching Atlanta for his family, Daryl fighting uphill with an arrow in his side, the Vatos group caring for abandoned elders. Weighing Nagel's objection that absurdity arises from our clashing subjective and objective perspectives, she concludes we cheer Rick shooting Sophia in the barn because subjective commitment stays noble even where objective meaning is nowhere to be found.

samples.book: 148 - Black Mirror and Philosophy - Dark Reflections
samples.title: The Death of Death
samples.relation: Reading Black Mirror's deaths through Bandersnatch's train ending, Be Right Back's AshBot, and San Junipero, the chapter uses Heidegger's presence-at-hand (Stefan's absent mother and rabbit remain present as possibilities he can act on) and Derrida's différance (the meaning of life and death is endlessly deferred as technology scrambles the presence/absence binary - Martha's simulated Ash, Liam's Grain deletions, Chris's guilt-haunted fiancée). A central section frames the whole debate as transhumanism - Kurzweil's three bridges to the posthuman against Fukuyama's warning that self-directed evolution replaces God - before Camus resolves the question of meaning: Kelly and Yorkie, like Sisyphus, create meaning by choosing their fate in a VR heaven that objectively matters nothing. Freud's Eros/Thanatos drives and Epicurus's 'death is nothing to us' close the chapter's question of whether to extend, hasten, or simply accept mortality.

samples.book: 106 - Peanuts and Philosophy - You're a Wise Man, Charlie Brown!
samples.title: 1. Charlie’s Eternal Quest for the Little Red-Haired Girl
samples.relation: The chapter reads Charlie Brown's lifelong, unconsummated longing for the never-seen Little Red-Haired Girl as a quest narrative without closure: like Beckett's Vladimir and Estragon he cannot act, and like Camus's Sisyphus he is an absurd hero whose dignity lies in persisting (the 2,120 lunch hours, the losing team, the pulled football) without reward. Using Lacan's account of desire - the wish for the Other's recognition, suspended between the demand for need and the demand for love - it argues Schulz keeps her invisible (except one 1998 silhouette) precisely so Charlie's desire stays in permanent suspension, like a Hitchcock MacGuffin. The closing section attacks The Peanuts Movie (2015) for betraying this existential vision: by showing the girl, rewarding Charlie with a kiss, and swapping Sisyphean defiance for 'believe in yourself' truisms, it delivers Sisyphus from his rock and so kills what made him admirable.

samples.book: 100 - Batman, Superman, and Philosophy - Badass or Boyscout_
samples.title: 8. Saints and Superheroes
samples.relation: Malloy uses the two heroes to explain supererogation - Urmson's "Saints and Heroes" puzzle of acts that are praiseworthy but not obligatory, like Batman rushing into burning buildings while Jimmy Olsen is under no duty to follow. Against the utilitarian and deontological denials that anything goes beyond duty (Singer's argument that Clark Kent's designer glasses are money he owes to charity, and Susan Wolf's Loving and Rational Saints whose lives, like Batman's broken retirements in The Dark Knight Returns and Batman Beyond, leave no room for anything worth living), he adopts Raz's view that a duty can be overridden by the moral reason of grave personal risk. Hence Batman's nightly risk-taking is a genuinely heroic choice, while Superman's powers make saving others morally required - so Batman is more truly a hero and Superman "just a good person with the powers of a living god."

samples.book: 004 - Buffy the Vampire Slayer and Philosophy - Fear and Trembling in Sunnydale
samples.title: Buffy As a Watcher (of Sorts)
samples.relation: Jason Kawal tests virtue ethics's 'act as the virtuous person would act' (Hursthouse's criterion) against Xander's 'What would Buffy do?': Buffy qualifies as a moral exemplar with heroic actions (nightly patrols, the 'Gift' plunge) and saintly sacrifices (the 'Doublemeat Palace' McJob for Dawn), but imitation fails — Xander lacks her abilities, tastes, relationships, and pure bravery, and stripping those away one by one turns Buffy into a copy of Xander. Worse, much of what Buffy does is supererogatory (Giles: 'She's a hero... She's not like us' in 'The Gift,' before killing Ben himself), so ordinary people are not morally required to do what she would do. His fix: ask what a fully informed, unimpaired virtuous observer — an 'angelic Buffy looking over our shoulders,' never drugged into 'Beer Bad' cave-Buffy — would deem right for us, given our own abilities and commitments.

samples.book: 089 - Steve Jobs and Philosophy - For Those Who Think Different
samples.title: Steve Jobs and Philosophy
samples.relation: Framed by Dickens's Jacob Marley, Walker asks whether Jobs deserved his posthumous accolades despite giving far less to charity than Bill Gates, and tests him under three frameworks. Aristotle's virtue ethics acquits him (character is judged holistically, and charity sits near the golden mean of open-handedness rather than being a checklisted duty); Mill's utilitarianism acquits him (his innovations maximized happiness and he violated no Harm Principle—though abandoning daughter Lisa counts as a harm); and Singer's drowning-child argument condemns him as near-morally-bankrupt for selling luxury gadgets while children starve. Kant both convicts (charity is an imperfect duty under the categorical imperative) and saves Jobs: treating the affluent individual as an end in himself, never merely a means to the destitute, blocks Singer's demand for giving to marginal utility.

samples.book: 168 - Heroes and Philosophy - Buy the Book, Save the World
samples.title: NOTES
samples.relation: Miles asks whether extraordinary power generates extraordinary obligations, testing Spider-Man's 'with great power comes great responsibility' against Claude the invisible thief and the heroes' reluctance. He uses Singer's principle of minimal obligation (Micah diverting the train from the infant; Claire's negligible risk in burning-building rescues; Hiro teleporting across distance) and Kant's perfect/imperfect obligation distinction (Niki choosing between saving Monica and mothering Micah; Noah Bennet lying to protect Claire) before deploying Fishkin's three 'explosion' objections: too many endangered people, too many capable heroes, and too many repeated rescues dilute obligation. He concludes the heroes went beyond the call of duty in saving New York, so saving the world could legitimately be their paid job, like lifeguards or soldiers.

samples.book: 098 - The Princess Bride and Philosophy - Inconceivable!
samples.title: 12. Should I Really Stop That Rhyming
samples.relation: Yuen uses the rhyming scene to analyze annoyance - rhyme hijacks Vizzini's attention, the Goldman/Morgenstern interruptions betray invested expectations, and fans' endless quotation is annoying through sheer repetition - concluding that annoyance is irreducibly relative and contextual. Aristotle's virtue theory supplies the moral frame: friendliness and wittiness, golden means between obsequiousness and surliness, buffoonery and boorishness, make being annoying a character flaw that damages the communal eudaimonia Aristotle takes the good life to require. Since these virtues may be supererogatory ideals rather than obligations, Yuen borrows Kant's imperfect duty to develop one's talents to explain why Inigo had to become a master swordsman - failing to hone the skill his one great goal demands would be a failure of self-respect.

samples.book: 192 - Superman and Philosophy - What Would the Man of Steel Do_
samples.title: 20. What It Takes
samples.relation: Argues Batman is more heroic than Superman because heroism requires supererogation and replicability: Wesley Autrey's subway rescue, done without obligation, outranks Sullenberger's 'just what we're trained for,' and unlike otherworldly Superman, Batman's human abilities let the rest of us imagine imitating him—heroism begets heroism, as Gordon's coat around young Bruce's shoulders helped make Batman. Batman is framed as the answer to the problem of evil in Susan Neiman's secular form: Rachel Dawes' challenge that good people do something, on the Rousseau side of the Enlightenment debate that morality must make evil intelligible (against Voltaire's refusal). Superman's overwhelming power makes relying on reason superfluous, so he becomes a symbol of what we can't be, while the Dark Knight models what we can.

samples.book: 115 - Iron Man vs. Captain America and Philosophy - Give Me Liberty or Keep Me Safe
samples.title: 2. Just Not the Hero Type (Not!)
samples.relation: McCrossin builds a six-part definition of heroism (moral, altruistic, atypical, supererogatory, replicable safeguarding) and tests it on Wesley Autrey versus Captain Sullenberger and a Super Autrey thought experiment: Iron Man's engineering-based feats are refinements of abilities we share and so inspire imitation, while there can only ever be one Captain America, making Tony the more heroic. The Sokovia Accords debate then contrasts two humilities, with Stark's willingness to accept oversight more heroic than Rogers' safest-hands-are-our-own confidence. The chapter closes by explaining why we invent super heroes at all through Susan Neiman's account of the problem of evil after twentieth-century atrocities, from the Stamford explosion to Charlie Spencer's death in Lagos.

samples.book: 207 - Wonder Woman and Philosophy - The Amazonian Mystique
samples.title: Notes
samples.relation: McCrossin builds a six-part definition of heroism (systematic, moral, altruistic, radically atypical, supererogatory, replicable safeguarding) using Wesley Autrey's Harlem subway save against Captain Sullenberger's Hudson landing, and argues Wonder Woman is genuinely heroic because her mission is voluntary and supererogatory - she wins the contest to leave Paradise Island and can retire to it at will, unlike a compulsory Superman. He then uses the demoted, powerless Diana Prince era with I Ching to show her deeds stay in principle replicable, like Batman's rather than Superman's. The payoff: Wonder Woman works only as a 'super hero' who inspires imitation, which is how 'we' answer the problem of evil - why innocent people suffer destructive, ruthless evil.

samples.book: 020 - Poker and Philosophy - Pocket Rockets and Philosopher Kings
samples.title: Poker and Philosophy
samples.relation: Ventimiglia mines No-Limit Hold'em for seven lessons philosophers also teach: we lack certain knowledge (Descartes' cogito is the famous quest for certainty, but philosophy's own history of disagreement proves uncertainty is the human condition), and like William James against Clifford we must still believe and act without the nuts — waiting for pocket aces while the blinds eat you alive is no strategy. Risking everything echoes Thoreau's escape from lives of quiet desperation, trusting hunches over arithmetic follows Thoreau and Peirce's sentimentalism, and the Darwin-and-Spencer competition of tournament poker hides a deeper cooperative social contract: get caught cheating and you are out of the game. It closes with Plato's four classic virtues from the Republic — wisdom, courage, moderation, and the justice of a balanced soul — as the perfection of a poker player.

samples.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
samples.title: Chapter 31 - “Piper in the Woods”
samples.relation: David Svolba hunts the 'distinct new idea' of 'Piper in the Woods': able-bodied garrison men on Asteroid Y-3 claim to have become plants so they can abandon jobs in a machine where 'the men are parts, and each has his job' - a radical but understandable response to lives devoted to meaningless, alienated labor whose ends they no longer identify with. Reading the story with Thoreau's warning that in a technological world we become 'tools of our tools', and likening the defectors to Timothy Leary's drop-outs, it presents Dick's tacit approval of the sun-basking plant-people as social criticism of a dehumanizing techno-industrial order that sees resistance only as laziness. The darker suggestion is that such a form of life is strangely hard to resist: escape collapses into self-imposed dehumanization, making the story perhaps a parable of drug-like escapism.

samples.book: 057 - Rush and Philosophy - Heart and Mind United
samples.title: Let Your Heart Be the Anchor and the Beat of Your Own Song
samples.relation: Berti reads Neil Peart's 1997-98 catastrophes (his daughter's car accident, his wife's cancer death) and the 55,000-mile Ghost Rider motorcycle exile through Sartrean existentialism: existence precedes essence, so with no God-given script Peart must author his own reactions, exactly as Sartre's student had to choose between mother and Resistance. The chapter tracks alienation ('I do not know who I am'), the duty to choose rather than lean on outside voices, and 'The Pass' as the voice telling a suicidal teenager to walk back from the razor's edge. Thoreau's Walden retreat supplies the model for the healing road, and Peart's own directives ('keep moving; kick your own ass, gently') enact 'Freewill' and 'Something for Nothing': we are the ones who choose, and the choice to live made all that followed (re-marriage, Vapor Trails, five more tours) possible.

samples.book: 169 - The Hobbit and Philosophy - For When You've Lost Your Dwarves, Your Wizard, and Your Way
samples.title: a4.xhtml
samples.relation: Bronson argues that walking is a philosophical practice against modern placelessness (Giddens' 'phantasmagoric' locality): Thorin survived Smaug's attack because as a youth he 'was a good adventurous lad, always on the move', and Tolkien's wise figures - slow, flower-stopping Tolkien himself, Gandalf who 'went to look ahead' and was brought back 'by looking behind', Bilbo's silent walking, Beorn's bear-travels - all practice attentive movement through place. He backs this with Montaigne's retirement to his tower and bringing thoughts back to the orchard, Thoreau's woods-walking that must be spiritual as well as physical, the Tao Te Ching's 'good travelers leave no tracks' and Zhuangzi's wandering virtues, and Buddhist walking meditation from the Buddha's wandering monks to Thich Nhat Hanh's peace steps.

samples.book: 060 - SpongeBob SquarePants and Philosophy - Soaking Up Secrets Under the Sea!
samples.title: Friends—Don’t Leave Home without ’Em
samples.relation: Greg Ahrenhoerster places SpongeBob in literary history between Transcendentalism and naturalism: 'Nature Pants' is a failed Walden — SpongeBob gives away his possessions for Jellyfish Fields but his 'jellyfish instincts' fail as badly as self-reliance in London's 'To Build a Fire' — while 'Squidville' shows the industrial city's cold indifference as in Crane's Maggie. 'Jellyfish Hunter' warns that trying to exploit nature (Krabs's jelly factory) invites nature's reprisal, since civilized beings without instinct are at nature's mercy. The naturalist moral, against Transcendentalist solitude, is that we survive only through each other: visit Jellyfish Fields, but bring a friend.

samples.book: 005 - The Lord of the Rings and Philosophy - One Book to Rule Them All
samples.title: The Lord of the Rings and Philosophy
samples.relation: Gregory Bassham distills six keys to happiness from Tolkien's hobbits and elves: delight in simple pleasures (Epicurus on natural pleasures, Thoreau's Walden simplicity), making light of troubles (Sam's star above Mordor, with Marcus Aurelius and Augustine on courage and hope), friendship (Aristotle's Nicomachean Ethics read against Sam, Merry, and Pippin refusing to let Frodo go alone), good character, beauty and creativity (Lothlórien versus Mordor, 'flow'), and wonder (Tom Bombadil, Frodo's 'recovery' of fresh vision at Cerin Amroth). He argues Tolkien thereby becomes a philosophical guide, pointing from the Shire and Rivendell to a richer, more joy-filled life.

samples.book: 059 - Halo and Philosophy - Intellect Evolved
samples.title: UNSC Briefing
samples.relation: Fred Van Lente's introduction argues that Master Chief is deliberately an empty shell—faceless, ageless, mostly silent—so the player's identity grafted onto him brings both to life at once in Halo: Combat Evolved's opening cryo-wakeup tutorial. He frames the book with Thoreau's Walden claim that philosophy is living simplicity, mapping it onto the Chief's ascetic soldier existence, and on Socrates: a game worth playing is worth examining, since the unexamined game is not worth playing. He closes with Aristotle's potentiality and actuality: the game actualizes the Chief as a kicker of alien ass, and the book actualizes the series' social and philosophical potential.

samples.book: 229 - The Philosophy of Sherlock Holmes
samples.title: The Industrious Sherlock Holmes
samples.relation: Bassham diagnoses Holmes as a workaholic against clinical criteria (obsessive work, few relationships, perfectionism, health neglect through fasting and cocaine), then traces the rise of the Protestant work ethic (Calvin, Weber, Carlyle) and its modern decline. Drawing on Thoreau's Walden critique of 'lives of quiet desperation,' Pieper on leisure, and the 'affluenza' literature, he distinguishes pathological from benign workaholism by warning signs and by motivation. He concludes Holmes is a pathological workaholic in his symptoms but redeemed by his noble, non-materialistic motive of fighting crime and achieving justice.
